# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

## Headline

Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable — field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB, AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it** the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms (`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels; the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a *minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up (P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification** (no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change, so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`); it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling, hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade / mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7 teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not** change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests; generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`, run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`, `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired; hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the weapon-leveling demonstration gym (parent AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J); `GymIndex` auto-discovers gyms; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the DOM-panel readout pattern.
- **Existing power-up gyms:** `GymPowerUpsCombat` (P3/P4/P6/P7, threats) and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level readout.

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and run-restart reset; and add game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared level path matches `PlayScene` for every power-up. Update the GDD/README references accordingly. No gameplay behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene: round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart, every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep; keeps the duplicate-body guard authoritative.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`); do not duplicate.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — only if a power-up level readout is added to the shared HUD; otherwise the readout stays gym-local (e.g. a `.gym-panel`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 — update the status/coverage sentence to name the shipped gym + tests.
- `README.md` — update the power-up leveling entry and its Coverage list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (primary):** a demo gym invites "while we're here" gameplay or tuning changes. Mitigation: this item is demonstration + tests only; record any balance/behaviour opportunity as a separate `discovered-from` item.
- **Threats vs legibility (assumption):** P3/P4/P6/P7 are only fully observable under threat; the demonstration gym may include an optional threat toggle **or** focus on the resolver/level readout and leave full combat behaviour to `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Chosen default: threat-free readout gallery, with an optional threat toggle only if needed for the parity tests.
- **HUD coupling (assumption):** the shared HUD has no power-up level readout; keep the new readout gym-local to avoid changing shared HUD behaviour.
- **Parity-test flakiness (risk):** booting two Phaser games per case under parallel load is slow; reuse the existing generous timeout pattern and a single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots.
- **Reset-on-run-restart (ambiguity):** the gym must offer a deterministic way to exercise `resetPowerUpLevels` for the reset test; expose a public restart/reset hook (test-only seam) rather than relying on a real GameOver.
- **Determinism (constraint):** all tests drive `tick(dt)`, no wall-clock.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups (parent / `discovered-from`). Ships the model this gym demonstrates.
- **AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Wire power-up level curves into `EffectsRegistry` and the shared effect path (predecessor; makes field pickups level up).
- **AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB** — Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 periodic bomb (range/frequency) level axes into the effect path.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the hold-full choice.
- **AH-0MUWGD0EN008T3TY** — P4 model: `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` replace `bombCharges` (supersedes the original P4 axis).
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** — Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration tests (the direct structural precedent; mirrors the same shape for weapons).
- **AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA** — Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining core-code duplication (the parity convention this item must respect).
- **AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR** — Test: P10 parity across `PlayScene`, `GymMinerals` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (precedent for real-gym parity tests).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed)
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** – Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed)
- **AH-0MU44MAAB0007BDD** – Documentation for combat spawning (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, assert, body (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, applies, assert, body, combatscene (+20 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, body, combatscene (+20 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was conducted: the seed context plus the shipped model, the wiring predecessors and the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent were sufficient to draft a clear brief (intake SKILL §4 — skip the interview when seed context suffices; AGENTS.md — do not ask unnecessary questions). Each apparent design choice is recorded below with the evidence that resolved it and the documented assumption taken where evidence was partial.

- **Q (resolved from the work item + precedent): Should this be a new dedicated gym or an extension of `GymPowerUpsCombat` / `GymPowerUpsUtility`?** — Answer: a **new** `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene. Evidence: the work-item title and description say "Add a gym scene"; the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent (AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J) established a dedicated leveling gym; `GymIndex` auto-discovers `Gym<Name>.ts`. Source: work-item description; `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- **Q (resolved from the work item): What is the parity-test scope?** — Answer: boot the **real** gym and assert the shared power-up level path is identical to `PlayScene`, not another minimal `EquivGymScene`. Evidence: the description explicitly requires game↔gym parity "for the shared power-up level path" and names the duplicate-body guard. Source: work-item description; `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): Should the gym include combat threats so P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour is fully observable?** — Answer (assumed, producer may override): threat-free readout gallery as the default, with an optional threat toggle only if the parity tests require observable combat behaviour. Evidence: `GymWeaponLeveling` is threat-free and demonstrates levels via a readout; `GymPowerUpsCombat` already owns the threat-based P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour. Source: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): What demonstrates "level" — a shared HUD readout or a gym-local panel?** — Answer (assumed): gym-local readout over `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`; avoid changing shared HUD behaviour. Evidence: the shared HUD has only a weapon-level readout; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the established gym-local `.gym-panel` pattern. Source: `src/ui/HUD.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): How does the gym exercise level reset?** — Answer (assumed): expose a deterministic public restart/reset hook on the gym scene so the reset test does not depend on a real GameOver sequence. Source: `Player.getPowerUpLevels` / `resetPowerUpLevels` (`src/entities/Player.ts`).
- **Observation:** the automated `find-related` report surfaced only generic matches (enemy gym, difficulty curve, combat-spawning docs); the higher-signal relationships above were found by manual worklog search and file inspection.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-14:** Plan skill executed. Decomposed into 3 children:
  1. AH-0MV7QKEEO006WFI1 — Implement GymPowerUpLeveling gym scene with integration tests (covers parent AC1–AC3)
  2. AH-0MV7QSZMW009OA75 — Game↔gym parity tests for the power-up level path (covers parent AC4)
  3. AH-0MV7QVOAG003U8AA — Document the GymPowerUpLeveling gym and verify the full suite (covers parent AC5–AC6)
- Dependency edges: parity depends on gym, docs depends on gym.
- Effort/risk: Small / Medium, score 6. Recommended 20.17h.
- Six automated review stages passed.
- AC coverage: all 6 parent ACs covered by children (see comment AH-C0MV7T60R9009Z2BR for matcher false-negative analysis).
- Four spurious auto-closed gap children (AH-0MV7SM4IX003WMAB, AH-0MV7SM4VS001GEWJ, AH-0MV7SM57F009S6QL, AH-0MV7SM5IA006OE9S) closed as duplicates.
- Parent stage set to `plan_complete`, status `open`.

Raised during intake of AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (field pickups must upgrade temporarily). The producer asked us to *consider creating a second power-up type* to represent consumable temporary grants (P6 Phase Shift charges, P7 Teleport stacks) whose unconsumed grants persist until consumed even after the temporary level window expires.

**discovered-from:AH-0MUX802450085VZZ**

## Goal
Evaluate whether consumable temporary grants should be modelled as a distinct power-up type/category rather than as a level that is temporarily raised. This is an *exploratory* task — no code behaviour change is committed until a design decision is made and accepted.

## Acceptance criteria
- A short design note is recorded on this item comparing (a) the level-based temporary model chosen in AH-0MUX802450085VZZ vs (b) a distinct consumable-grant type.
- Recommendation (with rationale) is recorded and the producing work item is linked.
- If a change is recommended, follow-up implementation work items are created; otherwise the item is closed as 'no change required'.

## Notes
- This item is NOT blocking AH-0MUX802450085VZZ, which proceeds with decision (b): unconsumed grants persist until consumed and are not removed on expiry.
## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — the shipped (a) temporary/permanent split: `tempStacks` / `permanentGrants`, effective vs permanent upgrade levels, consumable-grant persistence on expiry (AH-0MUX802450085VZZ).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — P6 Phase Shift charge / P7 Teleport stack grant-and-consume semantics.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpId` / power-up descriptor shape where any distinct power-up type/category would be introduced.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 — power-up/weapon model the design note must stay consistent with.

# Demo mode: any non-movement key returns to the main menu

*In attract/demo mode, pressing any key other than a movement key — including ESC — returns to the main menu, while a movement key (W/A/S/D per the configured bindings, or an arrow key) still takes over the run in place, and the pointer stays ignored.*

## Problem statement

The requester expects demo mode to behave like a classic arcade attract loop: **any deliberate keyboard input other than movement abandons the demo and returns to the main menu**. The shipped behaviour (AH-0MUYJRHMC0038RAS / AH-0MUYP6M6W006Z1AY, v0.1.10) deliberately narrowed this so that only **ESC** left the demo and **all other non-movement keys were ignored** — an operator could bump a random key without dropping an unattended attract loop into human control. That decision is now being revisited: the operator wants the stronger signal — a non-movement key is a deliberate "get me out" gesture and should return to the menu rather than being silently swallowed.

This is a **behaviour change to shipped, intentionally-designed behaviour**, not a new subsystem. The movement-key take-over stays exactly as shipped.

## Users

- **As an arcade operator running the attract loop**, I want a stray non-movement key (or a deliberate one) to take the cabinet back to the main menu cleanly, rather than being silently ignored while the demo keeps playing.
- **As a player who has just watched the demo**, I want to press a movement key (W/A/S/D or an arrow key) to take over and keep playing the current run, unchanged.
- **As a player or operator who wants to leave the demo**, I want **any** other key — including ESC — to return me to the main menu.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, the demo is running unattended and someone presses a random letter or the space bar — the cabinet returns to the main menu instead of the key doing nothing.
- As a player, the demo is running and I press **W** or the **up arrow** — I am now in control of the ship mid-run, exactly as before.
- As a player, the demo is running and I press **ESC** (or any other key) — I land back on the main menu.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Any non-movement key returns to the main menu.** While `PlayScene` is in demo mode, pressing a **non-movement keyboard key** (e.g. ESC, Space, Enter, Tab, letters/numbers, F-keys) leaves the demo and returns directly to `MenuScene` (`this.scene.start('MenuScene')`), abandoning the run without the game-over dwell or any scoring. ESC must **not** open the pause menu.
2. **AC2 — Movement keys still take over in place.** While in demo mode, pressing a **movement key** — W/A/S/D using the player's configured `moveUp`/`moveDown`/`moveLeft`/`moveRight` bindings, or an **arrow key** — calls `setDemoMode(false)` in place; the run continues and the keyboard then drives the ship. Rebinding movement keys is honoured. (Unchanged from AH-0MUYP6M6W006Z1AY AC2.)
3. **AC3 — Pointer/click remains ignored.** While in demo mode, a pointer/click does **not** take over and does **not** return to the menu; the demo keeps playing. (Unchanged from AH-0MUYP6M6W006Z1AY AC3.)
4. **AC4 — ESC/pause arbitration preserved.** In demo mode the existing ESC → `togglePause()` handler must not fire — exactly one action (return to menu) applies, and the pause menu never opens during a demo. ESC in non-demo play continues to toggle the pause menu, unchanged.
5. **AC5 — Unattended demo lifecycle unchanged.** With no input, a demo run still plays to completion and follows the existing demo lifecycle (auto `GameOverScene` demo dwell → return to the menu, non-scoring). The change must not affect this path.
6. **AC6 — Normal play unaffected.** Outside demo mode no take-over listener is registered; keyboard and pointer behaviour are byte-for-byte unchanged.
7. **AC7 — Listener cleanup.** The demo take-over listener is removed on take-over, on return-to-menu and on scene shutdown, so no listener leaks across sessions.
8. **AC8 — Tests.** Automated tests cover: a non-movement key returns to `MenuScene`; ESC returns to `MenuScene` and does not pause; a movement key still takes over in place; the pointer does not take over and does not return to the menu; normal play is unaffected; listeners are cleaned up.
9. **AC9 — Documentation.** README (attract/demo description and the run instructions) and the Game Design Document attract/demo "Take over" subsection are updated to describe "any non-movement key returns to the menu; movement keys take over; pointer ignored", and the affected code comments are corrected.
10. **AC10 — Quality gates.** Typecheck and build pass, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Demo-only change.** Only the demo/attract path may change behaviour; normal play must be unchanged (AC6).
- **Movement-key take-over is retained.** Do not remove the in-place take-over or the movement-key matching (`_isMovementKey`, `movementKeyNames`, arrow keys). Only the *non-movement* branch changes from "ignore" to "return to menu".
- **Gym↔game parity.** Take-over/demo mode is `PlayScene`-only (gyms have no demo mode); no divergence is expected. Confirm no shared-core (`src/scenes/core/`) change is required; if one is, apply it consistently.
- **Single source of movement keys.** Keep deriving the take-over key set from the same source as normal play (arrow keys + the resolved `moveUp`/`moveDown`/`moveLeft`/`moveRight` bindings), so custom bindings are honoured.
- **ESC/pause arbitration.** The existing ESC → `togglePause()` handler must not also fire while demo mode is on.
- **No new dependencies.**

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
  - `_enableDemoTakeOver()` (~line 3330) registers a single `keydown` handler that today branches: `event.key === this.pauseKeyName` (ESC) → `_disableDemoTakeOver()` then `scene.start('MenuScene')`; `_isMovementKey(event)` → `setDemoMode(false)` (take over); **everything else → ignored** (no-op). There is no `pointerdown` listener (removed by AH-0MUYP6M6W006Z1AY).
  - `_disableDemoTakeOver()` (~line 3379) removes the listener; called on take-over, on ESC-to-menu and on shutdown (`teardownRunState()`), so no cross-session leak.
  - `create()` (~line 767) registers the ESC/pause handler gated on `!this.demoMode`, so ESC does not pause while demoing.
  - `_isMovementKey(event)` / `_normaliseKeyName(key)` (~lines 3354–3376) match arrow keys plus `this.movementKeyNames` (resolved movement bindings).
  - `setDemoMode(demo)` (public, ~line 3306) turns demo on/off and enables/disables take-over.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — `startDemo()` starts `PlayScene` with `{ demo: true }`; the idle-attract timer restarts the demo after 15 s of menu inactivity (reset by any key or pointer input).
- Docs describing the current "only ESC leaves; every other key ignored" behaviour: `README.md` (~line 363 and the run instructions ~line 386) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §**Attract / demo mode**, "Take over" bullet (~line 214).
- Tests asserting the current non-movement-key no-op: `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` "AC3 — a non-movement key is ignored and the demo keeps playing" (~line 4350); `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` "AC3 — a non-movement key during the demo does not take over" (~line 594); `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` pointer no-take-over case (~line 437).

## Desired change

- In `_enableDemoTakeOver()` in `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, invert the fall-through branch: if the key is a **movement key**, take over in place (`setDemoMode(false)`); otherwise (including ESC and the pause key) **return to the main menu** — cleaning up the listener first (`_disableDemoTakeOver()` then `this.scene.start('MenuScene')`). A single branch now covers ESC and every other non-movement key.
- Remove the now-dead special-case comparison against `this.pauseKeyName` inside the demo handler (every non-movement key takes the same path). Keep the `!this.demoMode` gate in the `create()` ESC handler.
- Keep the `event.repeat` guard, the `_isMovementKey` helper, `movementKeyNames`, and the callback cleanup semantics unchanged.
- No pointer listener is added.
- Update `README.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md`, and the code comments in `PlayScene.ts`, to the new behaviour.
- Update the existing tests that assert a non-movement key is ignored to instead assert it returns to the menu, and keep the movement-key take-over, pointer-ignore and normal-play cases green.

### Implementation notes

1. `_enableDemoTakeOver()` handler becomes roughly:
   ```ts
   const handler = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
     if (event.repeat) return;
     if (this._isMovementKey(event)) {
       this.setDemoMode(false); // take over in place
       return;
     }
     // Any other key leaves the demo for the main menu.
     this._disableDemoTakeOver();
     this.scene.start('MenuScene');
   };
   ```
2. Delete the `event.key === this.pauseKeyName` branch (no longer needed — it is covered by the fall-through) unless keeping it improves clarity; the resulting behaviour is identical.
3. The `create()` pause handler stays gated on `!this.demoMode` (AC4).
4. Update the docstring of `_enableDemoTakeOver` to state the new contract.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **Edit**: invert the non-movement branch to return to `MenuScene`; update the demo handler docstring; keep cleanup/`_isMovementKey` semantics.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — **Edit**: change "a non-movement key is ignored" to "a non-movement key returns to `MenuScene`"; keep ESC→menu, movement-key take-over, pointer-ignored, normal-play and cleanup cases.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` — **Edit**: change the non-movement-key demo case from "does not take over" to "returns to the main menu".
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — **Edit**: keep the pointer no-take-over case; add/adjust a non-movement-key → live `MenuScene` case.
- `README.md` — **Edit**: attract/demo description (~line 363) and the run instruction (~line 386).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **Edit**: attract/demo "Take over" bullet (~line 214).

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- **Reverses a deliberate design decision (medium).** AH-0MUYJRHMC0038RAS intentionally ignored non-movement keys to protect an unattended attract loop. This change makes any keypress leave the demo. Mitigation: the operator has explicitly chosen this behaviour (see Appendix Q1(b)); record the reversal in the work item and docs so the rationale is traceable.
- **Test churn (low).** Several existing tests assert the non-movement-key no-op (`PlayScene.test.ts` AC3, `MenuScene.test.ts` AC3, `demoMode.integration.test.ts`). They must be updated to the new expectation rather than deleted; keep the movement/pointer/normal-play assertions intact.
- **ESC/pause double-fire (low).** Already mitigated by the `!this.demoMode` gate in `create()`; the demo handler returns to the menu only. Keep a regression test.
- **Pointer inconsistency (low).** Keyboard now returns to the menu, but the pointer stays ignored — an intentional asymmetry chosen by the operator (Appendix Q2(a)). Record it in the docs so it does not read as an oversight.
- **Scope-creep (low).** Changing the movement-key take-over, re-adding pointer take-over, or altering capture tooling are **out of scope**; record any such opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

**Assumptions (producer-validatable)**

- Returning to the menu abandons the demo run immediately — no game-over dwell and no scoring (consistent with the shipped ESC path).
- The movement-key set and the in-place take-over semantics are unchanged.
- The pointer deliberately remains ignored (operator choice).

## Related work

# Intake Brief: Automated Balancing

> **Headline:** Turn the existing same-seed evaluation harness into an
> automated-balancing framework that simulates hundreds of deterministic bot
> games against the real balance data files and reports full statistics, so
> tuning is driven by evidence instead of intuition.

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** epic · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

Balancing the game is currently a manual, point-in-time activity: a designer
edits `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` / `ship-config.csv` / `difficulty-curves.csv`,
reloads, watches a run, and guesses. The pieces to do better already exist — a
deterministic headless arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`), a metric/A-B layer
(`src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`), and a telemetry schema that already records
minerals, upgrades (`choice_selected`), kills (`enemy_killed`) and pickups —
but the arena is **not config-driven** (it hardcodes `scout/diver/phaser`, a
fixed fire cadence and radius), the metric layer does **not** aggregate
per-upgrade or per-archetype statistics, and there is no way to run a **batch
of hundreds of games** and read its aggregated distribution. We need a
framework that simulates many bot games, collects full balance statistics, and
reports them so balance can be tuned from evidence rather than intuition.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want to run hundreds of bot games
  after changing a balance value and get a statistical report (minerals,
  upgrades, kills, survival, wave reached), so I can see whether the change
  improved or hurt play before shipping it.
- **As the bot maintainer**, I want the simulated scenario to read the real
  balance data files, so a run reflects the tuning I just made (not a
  hardcoded copy).
- **As a producer**, I want a stable, reproducible artifact per batch, so a
  balance change can be reviewed and compared over time.
- **As a downstream consumer** (the human-play stats and periodic
  human-experience validation work items), I want one shared balance-statistics
  schema, so bot and human measurements are directly comparable.

## Acceptance criteria
- **Config-driven simulation.** A headless run consumes the real balance data (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `src/data/ship-config.csv`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` and/or the shared wave sequencer) through the existing config loaders, with no divergent copy of enemy/ship/wave stats. A test demonstrates that changing a CSV value changes the simulated outcome (e.g. enemy health/`shotProbability`).
- **Batch runner.** A documented command runs at least ~100 deterministic bot games (seeds × policy) in one invocation and completes in a practical time on a dev machine, emitting raw telemetry plus an aggregated report. Same seed + config + policy yields a byte-identical report.
- **Full balance statistics.** The report captures, per run and aggregated, at minimum: minerals collected, upgrades selected (per upgrade/choice id), enemies killed **per archetype**, asteroids destroyed, power-ups collected, avoidable hits, survival time, and wave/level reached — with distribution summaries (count, mean, median, min, max, std-dev) across games.
- **Human-readable + machine-readable output.** The batch writes stable JSON artifacts and prints (or writes) a human-readable balance summary; the statistics schema is versioned and shared, not duplicated.
- **Tests.** Pure aggregation, determinism and the config-driven arena are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
## Constraints

- **Determinism (preserve AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4 AC5).** Every run derives from a
  seed; no wall clock; the batch report is reproducible byte-for-byte.
- **Dev/eval only.** No production runtime impact and no addition to the
  shipped gameplay path; `src/ai/eval/` stays pure (no I/O, no wall clock);
  filesystem work stays in the Node shell (`scripts/evaluate.mjs`).
- **Single source of truth.** The arena must consume the shared config
  loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` / `enemyConfig.ts` /
  `difficultySequencer.ts`), never a second copy of enemy or ship stats.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The arena is a dev tool (like the gyms); any shared
  gameplay behaviour it exercises must come from the shared core
  (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/utils/movementModel.ts`), never a divergent copy.
- **No PII.** Reuse the existing telemetry schema and redaction policy.
- **Bounded resources.** Hundreds of runs must not exhaust memory; keep the
  per-run footprint small and stream/aggregate incrementally where possible.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — deterministic headless arena; hardcoded
  `['scout','diver','phaser']`, fixed `ENEMY_FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS`,
  `HOSTILE_RADIUS`, and `SHIP_CONFIG`; not config-driven.
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — `MetricPoint`/`MetricAggregate` with score,
  survival, minerals-per-minute, power-ups, enemies/asteroids destroyed,
  avoidable hits, input cadence, dodge rate; **no per-upgrade or per-archetype
  breakdown and no percentile distribution**.
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` / `cli.ts` / `report.ts` — single/A-B evaluation over
  a small seed list (`--seeds N`, default 3); reports stored as JSON/JSONL.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — Node shell (Vite SSR module loader, file I/O).
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — documents the existing harness.
- `src/data/*.csv` + `src/core/configStore.ts` — the real, editable balance
  data and its loader.
- Telemetry already emits `enemy_killed {archetype,x,y}`, `pickup {kind,id}`,
  `mineral_collected {total}`, `choice_selected {index,id}`, `wave_*`,
  `level_cleared`.

## Desired change

Turn the eval harness into an automated-balancing framework:

1. Make the headless arena **config-driven** from the real balance data.
2. Add a **batch runner** for hundreds of deterministic games.
3. Extend the metric layer with the **full balance-statistics schema** and
   distribution summaries (per-upgrade, per-archetype, wave reached, etc.).
4. Emit **JSON + human-readable** balance reports; version the schema so human
   and periodic-validation consumers can share it.
5. Document how to run a batch and interpret the report; cover it with tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — make the arena consume real enemy/ship/wave data.
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — add balance-statistics extraction + distributions.
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — extend statistics/report types (versioned schema).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — include the new statistics and batch summary.
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — batch runner over many games/seeds.
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` and `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — CLI flags for batch size,
  statistics output and report.
- `src/ai/eval/index.ts` — public surface for the shared statistics schema.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` / `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` /
  `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — consumed as the single source of truth.
- `src/ai/eval/*.test.ts` — tests for aggregation, determinism, config-driven
  behaviour.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` (and/or a new `docs/BALANCING.md`) — how to run a batch
  and read the report.

## Risks, assumptions and mitigations

- **Assumption:** the "reasonably accurate human-like" bot is the `competent`
  policy; the batch runner defaults to it.
- **Assumption:** "hundreds of games" means roughly 100–1000 deterministic
  runs (seeds × policies) per batch.
- **Fidelity risk:** the headless arena is a simplification, so bot balance
  stats may not match the shipped game. *Mitigation:* make it config-driven,
  document the fidelity boundary, and pair it with the human-play statistics
  and periodic human-experience validation items below.
- **Environment risk:** loading CSV-backed config under Node/Vite SSR may need
  verification. *Mitigation:* prototype config loading first (spike within the
  item) before building the statistics layer on top.
- **Scope-creep risk:** human-play collection and periodic human-experience
  validation are **separate work items** (below) — do not fold them into this
  epic. Any further opportunities get their own linked item.

## Related work

- **Same-seed evaluation harness: metrics, A/B, side-by-side** (AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4) — the foundation this builds on.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ) — recording/analysis path reused for human stats.
- **Telemetry: per-tick integration with no-op contract** (AH-0MUZQEDW9002KHRN) and the telemetry framework (AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO).
- **Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling** (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP) — balance-rule consumer.
- **Tune enemy balance: reduce scout durability and tank firing** (AH-0MULW9HNC001GVCY) — the manual pass this automates.
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — shares the statistics schema.
- **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — depends on this epic.
- **Reduce bullet speed of enemies** (AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ) — a completed tuning pass on `enemy-configs.csv` (bulletSpeed/lifetime) that this framework would measure instead of eyeballing.
- **Write tests for new game scenes and systems** (AH-0MU732AJW005RTG1) — precedent for the test expectations on the new stats layer.
- Docs: `docs/EVALUATION.md`, `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Integration/scope.** How should this relate to the existing same-seed harness?
  - **Answer (operator):** A — extend the existing harness (`src/ai/eval/`, `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`) with a batch/statistics layer. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Fidelity / what gets simulated.** What should the simulation actually run?
  - **Answer (operator):** A — extend the existing headless arena to be config-driven from `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv` and `ship-config.csv`, so tuning edits are measurable. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Statistics and output.** Which statistic set/format?
  - **Answer (operator):** A — full stats (minerals, per-upgrade choice counts, per-archetype kills, wave/level reached, survival-time distribution, avoidable hits) as per-seed + aggregate distributions, output as JSON artifacts and a human-readable report. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 — Human player data.** Could the same data be collected from human player games?
  - **Answer (operator):** Yes — create a **high-priority** work item to collect the same data in human player games, **dev mode only**. Created as **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5 — Periodic human-experience validation.** Should there be a check against the intended experience?
  - **Answer (operator):** Yes — create another work item, **dependent on both** this framework and the human-play stats item, to periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience. Created as **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775), with dependency edges to AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW and AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN. Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX** – Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support (completed)
- **AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L** – Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids (completed)
- **AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ** – Reduce bullet speed of enemies (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muy08xld009k4w4, ac5, acceptance, accurate, activity (+354 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muwz5gst003nmfq, 0mv29xq0h009p9wp, ac5, accurate, activity (+320 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muwz5gst003nmfq, 0mv29xq0h009p9wp, ac5, actually, add (+290 more)

---

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-14: Decomposed into 6 features (schema+aggregation, config-driven arena, batch runner, report+CLI, docs, acceptance verification). Coverage review verified at 100% (proceed). Note: tree-coverage auto-close placeholder children were removed and replaced with explicit 'Covers epic ACn' bullets.

# Bot steering model to consume live ShipConfig thruster values — Intake Brief

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** task (model plumbing/refactor, no new user-facing capability)

## Problem statement

The demo/competent bot's steering and forward model use hard-coded thruster
constants (`playerSpeed: 175`, `frictionDeceleration: 100`, and no reverse
values at all) instead of the player ship's live `ShipConfig`, so a change to
the player's thruster configuration is never picked up by the bot. This makes
the demo bot physically wrong against a tuned ship (wrong stopping distances,
wrong assumed cruise speed, and no representation of the reverse thruster's
acceleration/max speed).

## Users

- **Player watching the attract/demo** — expects the bot to fly the *same ship
  physics* the player configured, so the demo is a faithful preview of the
  game.
- **Developer / designer tuning ship config** — wants the demo bot to react
  correctly when thruster values are edited, so tuning can be validated
  against a skilled pilot.

Example user stories:

- As a player who tuned high friction, the bot stops within the predicted
  margin instead of sliding past, so the demo looks skilled with my ship.
- As a designer editing `frictionDeceleration`/`maxSpeed`, the demo bot's
  steering and stopping behaviour tracks the change without code edits, so I
  can validate tuning in a gym/run.
- As a player who disabled or re-tuned the reverse thruster, the bot's
  reverse braking uses my configured acceleration and speed cap, so the demo
  never contradicts the handling I experience.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Live thruster config in the snapshot.** `BotSnapshot` carries the
   player's live thruster configuration — forward `thrustAcceleration`,
   `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration`, and reverse `enabled` /
   `reverseAcceleration` / `reverseMaxSpeed` — sourced from the live
   `Player`/`ShipConfig` via `buildBotSnapshot`, not from tunables. The
   existing demo path (`PlayScene._advanceDemoBot` → `buildBotSnapshot(this)`)
   picks it up automatically with no hard-coded physics in the decision layer.
2. **AC2 — Steering/forward model consumes live values.** The steering
   candidate prediction (`evaluateDirection` player-speed term) and the
   forward-model thrust decision (`mayThrust` friction stopping distance)
   use the snapshot's live values; the tunables `playerSpeed` /
   `frictionDeceleration` are demoted to **defaults/overrides** (fallback when
   the snapshot carries no config, and overridable via GymBotTuning), never
   authoritative. **Precedence (pending producer confirmation): live
   ShipConfig wins for physics terms when present (option (a)); explicit gym
   overrides otherwise.**
3. **AC3 — Reverse thrust represented in the model.** Reverse braking is gated
   and modelled with the live reverse values: `asteroidsReverseEnabled`
   (already respected at snapshot level), `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration`
   and `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` feed the reverse forward-model (brake
   distance under reverse acceleration and/or reverse speed cap) instead of
   being absent. The existing `mayReverse` tuning gates
   (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`, `reverseRetreatRange`) remain tunables.
4. **AC4 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour change is applied consistently to
   the shipped game (`PlayScene` + shared core) and the gym scenes that
   exercise the bot (e.g. `GymBotTuning`), sharing the same snapshot/steering
   code — no divergent copy.
5. **AC5 — Testing & validation.** Unit tests cover (a) a custom thruster
   config changing the bot's steering/stopping/reverse decisions vs the
   defaults, and (b) the fallback path with no config in the snapshot
   (unchanged behaviour vs today). At least one test pins the pure decision
   layer consuming live values. **Full project test suite must pass with the
   new changes.**
6. **AC6 — Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and
   any relevant wiki/docs entries.

## Constraints

- The decision layer stays **pure and deterministic** — the snapshot is the
  only runtime input; no reading ship state from inside steering functions.
- Behaviour must be applied consistently to gyms and game (repo-wide
  duplicate-body guard + gym-parity docs assertion enforce this).
- Tunables must remain overridable (persisted `GymBotTuning` config and its
  `toCompetentOverrides` mapping) — overrides still win over live config
  where they exist, matching the current tuning seam.
- `assumedBulletSpeed` (enemy-bullet speed for fire-tell prediction) and
  `firePredictionHorizon` are **out of scope** — they model enemy bullets, not
  the player's ship, and stay tunables.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` hard-codes `playerSpeed: 175` and
  `frictionDeceleration: 100`; reverse braking has tuning gates
  (`reverseBrakeEnabled`, `reverseImminentOvershootGap`, `reverseRetreatRange`)
  but **no** reverse acceleration/max-speed in the model.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` uses `t.playerSpeed` in
  `evaluateDirection` (candidate-speed prediction) and
  `t.frictionDeceleration` in `mayThrust` (stopping distance); `mayReverse`
  gates on tunables only.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` exposes only position/velocity on `BotPlayer`
  (`x, y, vx, vy`) plus a snapshot-level `reverseEnabled` boolean; there is no
  thruster-physics field.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` holds the fleet thruster values in
  `_baseConfig`/`_config` (`thrust`, `maxSpeed`, `friction`, `reverseEnabled`,
  `reverseAcceleration`, `reverseMaxSpeed`) but exposes only
  `getRotationConfig()` and `isReverseEnabled()` publicly — no getter for the
  thruster physics.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_advanceDemoBot` already routes
  `buildBotSnapshot(this)` into the brain, so a snapshot change flows through
  automatically.

## Desired change

- Add thruster-physics fields to `BotPlayer` (or a nested `thruster` object)
  in `botSnapshot.ts`, populated from a new Player getter
  (e.g. `getThrusterConfig()` returning forward thrust/max speed/friction and
  reverse enabled/acceleration/max speed — mirroring `getRotationConfig`).
- In `steering.ts`, read live values from the snapshot/world for the
  candidate-speed term and the friction/reverse stopping model, falling back
  to the (renamed/documented as defaults) tunables when absent.
- Update `tunables.ts` defaults and doc comments to mark
  `playerSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration` (and any new reverse physics defaults)
  as fallback defaults + tuning overrides, not the ship's truth.
- Keep `update`-seam behaviour identical when no config is present (fallback
  equals today's constants).

## Key Files

- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — Add live thruster config to the snapshot and `BotPlayer`; update the `BotSnapshotScene`/`BotPlayerSource` structural seams.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — New public getter for thruster physics (forward + reverse), mirroring `getRotationConfig()`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `evaluateDirection`, `mayThrust`, `mayReverse` consume live values with tunable fallback.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — Demote physics constants to defaults/overrides; doc updates.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — Ensure `BotWorld.player` carries the config (it derives from the snapshot), and any reverse forward-model terms.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Demo path (already wired via `buildBotSnapshot`); verify no other hard-coded thruster use in the bot seam.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — Parity: verify the tuning overrides still win over live config.
- Tests: `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`, `competentBot.test.ts`, and `src/ai/botSnapshot` builder tests.
- Docs: `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1J0OHP0072XA5 — Bot to use the reverse thrusters** (parent; AC4 of
  that item explicitly defers "numeric customisation of the bot's *model* to
  live thruster values" to this item).
- **AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 — Overuse of the reverse thrusters** (reverse reserved
  for trouble/correction — this item must preserve those semantics).
- **AH-0MV4D7LAD009XYR0 — Gym scene for AI bot tuning** (`GymBotTuning`,
  persisted tunables seam).
- **AH-0MV2JT18K006YU35 — Reverse intent and enable-flag plumbing** (the
  `reverseEnabled` snapshot field this item extends with numeric values).
- **AH-0MV13LXOR001X15X — Config fields for the reverse thruster** (source of
  the `asteroidsReverse*` `ShipConfig` fields this item consumes).
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md** (AC4
  parity convention and the repo-wide duplicate-body guard that enforces it).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Fallback equivalence must be exact.** With the default ship config
  (`MAX_SPEED=175`, `FRICTION_DECELERATION=100` in `constants.ts`) the
  fallback values match today's tunables (`playerSpeed: 175`,
  `frictionDeceleration: 100`) exactly, so a ship running defaults must behave
  bit-for-bit as today. Any regression here is invisible-but-harmful to the
  demo bot.
- **Tuning-seam precedence (scope tension).** The tuning gym
  (`tuningFields.ts`) exposes `playerSpeed` and `frictionDeceleration` as
  sliders. If live `ShipConfig` becomes authoritative for physics terms, those
  two sliders become no-ops whenever a ship config is present (the live game
  always has one). Mitigation: record the expected precedence in the ACs
  (option (a) live-wins recommended) and flag the now-inert sliders as a
  follow-up work item rather than expanding scope here.
- **Assumption — `maxSpeed` is the live proxy for the candidate-speed term.**
  `playerSpeed` (assumed cruise speed for candidate-direction prediction)
  maps to `ShipConfig.maxSpeed`; the default value (175) already equals the
  tunable, so this is behaviour-preserving at defaults. If the intent were a
  *fraction* of max speed (cruise < cap), note that the current 175 is the
  full cap — the implementer should keep the default-equivalence property.
- **Scope-creep guard.** `assumedBulletSpeed` / `firePredictionHorizon`
  (enemy-bullet modelling) and rotation physics (already live via
  `getRotationConfig`, AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98) are out of scope; any further
  tuning-surface changes (e.g. deprecating sliders) are recorded as linked
  work items, not added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required — the seed context (item description, parent
AH-0MV1J0OHP0072XA5 AC4 note, and the competent-bot framework docs) plus repo
evidence (`tunables.ts`, `steering.ts`, `botSnapshot.ts`, `Player.ts`,
`configTypes.ts`) were sufficient to draft the brief.

- Q: "Which `ShipConfig` values feed the bot model?" — Answer (research):
  `thrustAcceleration`, `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration`,
  `asteroidsReverseEnabled`, `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration`,
  `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` (see `src/core/configTypes.ts`). Source: repo
  inspection (Player `_baseConfig` mapping, `getRotationConfig()` precedent).
- Q: "Do `playerSpeed` / `frictionDeceleration` disappear?" — Answer
  (research, from the item description): no — they become **defaults /
  overrides** (fallback for absence, overridable via GymBotTuning), never
  authoritative. Source: item description line "Update tunables to be
  defaults/overrides rather than authoritative values."
- Q: "Is `assumedBulletSpeed` (enemy-bullet speed) in scope?" — Answer
  (research): no — it models enemy bullets, not the player's ship. Source:
  `steering.ts` (fire-tell lead) and `worldModel.ts`
  (`assumedBulletSpeed`). Recorded as an out-of-scope constraint.
- Q: "When live ShipConfig is present, what wins for `playerSpeed` /
  `frictionDeceleration` (also exposed as tuning-gym sliders)?" — Answer
  (producer reply pending): **option (a) live config wins for physics terms**
  is recommended (matches "live values picked up automatically"); the gym

# Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Intake:** AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP · **Discovered from:** AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7

## Problem statement

The enemy classification system (`movementClass`/`attackClass` added to
`src/data/enemy-configs.csv` by **Enemy classification system for balanced
wave design** (AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7)) is descriptive and validated, but nothing
consumes it yet. This item makes the classification *actionable*: the runtime
wave generator enforces classification-based balance rules for generated
(`curve`/`dynamic`) waves, and the same rule definitions are exposed as a pure
validator so balance is testable and auditable.

## Users

- **Wave designer / producer** — composes and reviews campaign waves and wants
  generated waves to respect balance rules without manual review.
- **Developer / AI agent** — needs pure, unit-tested rule functions and clearly
  documented tunable constants so rules can be reasoned about and extended.

Example user stories:

- *As a wave designer, I want the wave generator to enforce classification
  rules (opening waves formation-only; no all-chaser wave; bounded ranged mix)
  so that generated waves are balanced without manual review.*
- *As a reviewer, I want the same rules available as a pure validator so the
  shipped campaign can be audited in CI.*

## Summary of interview decisions (producer, intake round 1)

- **Q1 (enforcement model) = c.** Hard constraints in the generator *and* a
  pure audit validator, both reusing the same rule definitions (single source
  of truth).
- **Q2 (rule scope) = a.** All three user-story rules ship in this item:
  R1 opening waves formation-only; R2 no all-chaser wave; R3 bounded mix of
  ranged attackers.
- **Q3 (fixed-wave scope) = a.** Rules apply to **generated** (`curve` /
  `dynamic`) waves only. Hand-authored `fixed` waves are intentionally exempt
  at runtime and are not audited in tests; existing `fixed` waves must not
  break.

## Rules (tentative definitions, to be pinned in implementation)

- **R1 — Opening-wave purity.** Opening waves (the `dynamic` onboarding slots,
  waves 1–2 of levels 1–2, matching the existing `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION`
  positions; named constant) contain only archetypes with
  `movementClass ∈ {formation, diver}` — chasers/patrollers/roamers are
  excluded. *Interpretation note:* "melee" in the user story is read as
  non-chaser; `attackClass` is not constrained because onboarding waves are
  no-fire (existing openers scout/diver/swarm are `projectile`-class).
- **R2 — No all-chaser wave.** No generated wave may be composed entirely of
  archetypes with `movementClass === 'chaser'`.
- **R3 — Bounded ranged mix.** No generated wave may be composed entirely of
  ranged attackers (`attackClass ∈ {projectile, beam, area}`); every generated
  wave includes at least one `contact` (non-ranged) group ("bounded mix"
  implemented as a ranged-share cap).

**Precedence:** balance rules are **hard constraints** for generated waves — a
violating composition is never produced; the sequencer minimises difficulty
error within the rule-constrained candidate space (rules win over exact target
match).

## Existing state

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — all 18 rows carry `movementClass` /
  `attackClass`; codec validates and coerces them (AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7).
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — runtime auto-sequencer: picks candidate
  archetypes by `enemyDifficulty` score to hit a target curve; composition
  only, no classification awareness. Has a per-level archetype cap
  (`MAX_ARCHETYPE_PER_LEVEL`).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (`curve`/`fixed`/`dynamic`
  modes, seeded `dynamic` jitter); hard-coded `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION` selects
  opening archetypes by **key** (`scout`/`diver`/`swarm`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — dev-utility preview of the sequencer
  output (shared core ⇒ parity by construction).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1.4 — documents classification as
  data-only and names this item as its consumer.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure rule module (e.g. `src/core/waveBalance.ts`): R1–R3 as functions
   over a wave's groups (archetype → classification via the config store /
   defaults) with named, documented, tunable constants; each rule returns
   pass/fail plus a human-readable message; a validator audits an arbitrary
   wave list using the same functions.
2. Enforce the rules as hard constraints in `difficultySequencer.ts`
   composition (candidate filtering and/or composed-wave rejection), so no
   generated wave violates them.
3. Replace the key-based `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION` with a classification-driven
   R1 expression (or guard the curated pool with R1) to remove the
   archetype-key duplication.
4. Verify the shipped campaign still satisfies the difficulty-curves (target
   error may grow where rules bind; record in docs).
5. Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1.4 (or a new §1.5) with
   the rules, constants and how to tune them; add unit tests.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — Rule module.** A pure, shared module defines R1–R3 as documented
   functions with named tunable constants; each function takes a wave's groups
   (resolved to classifications) and returns pass/fail with a message; a
   validator audits a list of waves reusing the same functions.
2. **AC2 — Generator enforcement.** The runtime auto-sequencer enforces R1–R3
   as hard constraints for generated (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves: unit tests
   prove the sequencer never produces a violating wave for the default
   candidate pool across a range of target curves.
3. **AC3 — Opening curation migrated.** The key-based `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION`
   in `sequencedLevels.ts` is replaced or guarded by the classification-driven
   R1, removing duplicated archetype-key logic.
4. **AC4 — Campaign audit + determinism.** A pure validator reuses the rules;
   a test audits the shipped campaign generated from `defaultDifficultyCurves()`
   and confirms no generated wave violates R1–R3 (fixed waves exempt per
   Q3=a), while seeded-`dynamic` reproducibility is preserved.
5. **AC5 — Gym↔game parity.** Rules live in the shared core consumed by both
   the game's campaign builder and the `GymCurveSequencer` preview, so parity
   holds by construction (not a divergent copy).
6. **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1.4
   (or new §1.5) documents the rules, constants, tuning guidance and the
   enforcement/audit design; all related documentation is updated (code
   comments, README, wiki/docs entries).
7. **AC7 — Testing / validation.** Unit tests cover each rule (pass, violation
   rejected, borderline), rule enforcement in the sequencer, the campaign
   audit, and determinism. **Full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.**

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** rules must run the same code in game and gym (shared
  core only; see AGENTS.md).
- **Single source of truth (Q1=c):** generator enforcement and the audit
  validator consume the *same* rule functions — no duplicated rule logic.
- **Fixed waves exempt:** authored `fixed` waves are never sequenced and must
  not be altered or rejected (Q3=a).
- **Determinism/seeding:** generated waves stay reproducible for a given seed;
  rules introduce no randomness.
- **Backward compatibility:** classification fields already validated by the
  codec; this item only *consumes* them.
- **UK English** in all docs and comments.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — rule/curve tension.** Enforcing hard rules may make a generated
  wave miss its `targetDifficulty` (rules win over exact target match).
  Mitigation: document the resulting target error, re-check the shipped
  campaign audit test, and retune the curve only if a wave becomes
  degenerate (no producer revert needed for minor error growth).
- **Risk — scope creep.** If R3's "bounded ranged mix" quota proves hard to
  define cleanly across all pool archetypes, implement R1+R2 first and record
  R3's exact quota as a named constant default that tests may relax — but
  keep all three rules in this item per Q2=a.
- **Assumption — "melee" reading.** In R1, "formation/melee" is read as
  `movementClass ∈ {formation, diver}`; `attackClass` is not constrained for
  openers because onboarding waves are no-fire (existing openers are
  `projectile`-class). Recorded above; adjust if the producer reads "melee"
  by `attackClass`.
- **Assumption — shared core.** Balance rules have no Phaser dependency and
  run under Vitest (like `enemyDifficulty`), enabling pure unit tests.
- **Assumption — fixed-wave audit.** Per Q3=a, `fixed` waves are *not*
  audited in tests; only generated waves are.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/waveBalance.ts` *(new)* — pure R1–R3 rule functions, constants and
  validator.
- `src/core/waveBalance.test.ts` *(new)* — per-rule unit tests.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — enforce rules as hard constraints during
  composition.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — migrate `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION` to
  classification-driven R1; campaign audit wiring.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.test.ts` / `difficultySequencer.variety.test.ts`
  — rule-enforcement tests.
- `src/waves/campaignInvariants.test.ts` (or new audit test) — campaign obeys
  R1–R3.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §1.4/§1.5 rules + tuning docs.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7** — Enemy classification system (blocker, completed):
  delivers the consumed fields.
- **AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K** — Enemy difficulty index (design-time scoring used
  by the sequencer).
- **AH-0MV2SGIX5005PFJT** — per-level archetype variety cap in the sequencer
  (precedent for composition constraints).
- **AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B** — curated opening pools (the key-based logic R1
  replaces).
- **AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X** — runtime auto-sequencer item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the rules be enforced?" — Answer (producer): "(c) Both —
  hard rules in generation, reusing the same rule definitions in an audit
  validator (single source of truth)." Source: interactive reply, intake
  round 1.
- Q2: "Which rules belong in this item?" — Answer (producer): "(a) All three
  user-story examples: opening waves formation-only; no all-chaser wave;
  bounded ranged-attacker mix." Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q3: "Do rules apply to authored `fixed` waves too, or only generated ones?"
  — Answer (producer): "(a) Only generated (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves —
  `fixed` waves are hand-authored and intentionally exempt." Source:
  interactive reply, intake round 1.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUGCSQKU003R4WW** – Update documentation — asteroid spawn mechanic (completed)
- **AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW** – Automated Balancing (open)
- **AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA** – Mineral rules tunables and per-enemy mineral count (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv29nwi1007nkn7, acceptance, actionable, add, added (+108 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv29nwi1007nkn7, add, added, archetypes, attack (+100 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mv29nwi1007nkn7, add, added, archetypes, attack (+93 more)


## Plan (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP)

Decomposition produced by the plan skill. Pre-check: effort Medium / risk Medium → full planning required. Approval gate: `request_approval=false` → no approval pause. Duplicate-work detection: none found. Six automated review stages run (sequencing/scope/AC/parity), see comments.

Features (test-first order; each a vertical slice):

1. **Rule contract tests + classification fixtures** (task) — `waveBalance.test.ts`: R1–R3 pass/violation/borderline suites, validator contract, effective-attack semantics (no-fire ⇒ contact, producer Q1), classification fixture; red until F2.
2. **Pure wave-balance rule module R1–R3 + validator** (feature, AC1) — `src/core/waveBalance.ts`: pure functions, named tunable constants, pass/fail + message, audit validator; single source of truth consumed by sequencer, campaign audit and gym.
3. **Sequencer hard-constraint enforcement** (feature, AC2) — `difficultySequencer.ts` filters/rejects so no generated wave violates R1–R3; rules win over exact target match; determinism preserved.
4. **Classification-driven opening curation** (feature, AC3) — `sequencedLevels.ts`: `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION` guarded by R1, curated sub-selection kept as data (producer Q2=b).
5. **Campaign audit, determinism and gym↔game parity** (task, AC4/AC5) — validator audits the shipped campaign; seeded-`dynamic` reproducibility; parity by construction with `GymCurveSequencer`.
6. **Documentation + full-suite validation** (docs, AC6/AC7) — ENEMY_DESIGN doc §1.4/§1.5 rules/constants/tuning; all docs updated; full suite passes.

Dependencies: F2←F1, F3←F2, F4←F2, F5←{F3,F4}, F6←F5.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-14 — Decomposed into 6 features; AC coverage review applied; children created; effort/risk recomputed per child; stage → `plan_complete`.


## Appendix additions (plan interview round 1)

- Q4: "R3 conflicts with R1 on no-fire opening waves — every formation/diver archetype is ranged. Exempt no-fire waves from R3?" — Answer (producer): "a formation group with shoot turned off is a contact group" → R3 treats the wave's *effective* attack: when `shootEnabled === false` all groups count as `contact`, so no-fire waves are R3-compliant by construction (resolves R1↔R3; no new classification needed for this item; producer mused on a future `formation+ranged` axis — recorded, not in scope here). Source: interactive reply, plan round 1. Final: effective-attack semantics.
- Q5: "AC3 'replaced or guarded' — full replacement widens openings to every formation/diver candidate and risks degenerate waves." — Answer (producer): "(b) Guarded replacement — derive the opening pool from R1, keep the curated sub-selection (`scout`/`diver`/`swarm`) as data for degenerate-wave safety, removing only duplicated classification logic." Source: interactive reply, plan round 1. Final: guarded replacement (Q2=b).
