# Variety in weapon graphics (AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE) — intake brief

## Headline

Make every projectile in the game visually distinct and juicy: give each of the 11 player weapons and every enemy attack its own code-drawn bullet shape, per-weapon VFX (muzzle flash, trail, impact) and SFX cues (fire + impact) — delivered as an epic with one child work item per weapon.

## Problem statement

Every projectile in AI Hell currently renders as a plain filled circle ("dot"), so a cannon pellet, a laser beam and a boss bullet are visually indistinguishable and firing feels flat. Each weapon's in-flight look should communicate what it does — the laser should be a line/beam, the rocket a missile, the nova an expanding ring — with matching sound and impact feedback that makes the weapon feel unique.

## Users

- **Player** — reads on-screen weapon identity at a glance during dense bullet-hell action; feels the difference between weapons when firing and when shots connect.
- **Developer** — benefits from one shared, parity-safe rendering seam so the game and every gym stay identical (repo gym↔game parity rule).

## Example user stories

- As a player, I want the Wave Laser to render as a visible neon beam (line), not a dot, so I can read its piercing column at a glance.
- As a player, I want each weapon's shots to have a distinct shape, colour, trail and hit effect, so the weapon I'm holding is obvious from what's on screen.
- As a player, I want a clear impact cue (flash + sound) when my shots hit, so hits feel responsive rather than silent.
- As a player facing enemy fire, I want each enemy archetype's projectiles to look like they belong to that enemy (a Scout pellet vs a Tank shell vs a Boss pulse), so I can parse the bullet field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Every player weapon is visually unique in flight.** Each of the 11 catalogue weapons (`cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova, mortar, arc`) has a distinct code-drawn projectile shape and/or per-shot VFX that differs from every other weapon; a doc/roster test asserts catalogue-wide uniqueness. The Wave Laser (and Dual) must render as a line/beam, **not** a dot.
- **Every enemy attack has its own projectile identity.** One child per enemy weapon: Scout/Invader aimed shot, Diver spread burst, Tank radial, Phaser radial, Swarm burst, Raider shot, Boss spread, Boss spiral, Boss pulse, Boss desperation, Capturer tractor beam, and Orbital-Strike falling shell — each with a distinct shape/colour/feel reflecting its archetype and gated by its existing fire behaviour (visuals/feel only; firing logic, speeds, intervals and patterns unchanged).
- **Per-weapon game feel.** Each weapon/attack child adds VFX **and** SFX for both fire and impact (muzzle flash / launch cue, trail where appropriate, impact flash + hit sound), consistent with the code-drawn neon aesthetic and the existing baked-cue audio pipeline (ToneForge `playCue`).
- **Gym↔game parity.** Every gameplay-visual change is applied through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, shared entities/utils) and consumed identically by the relevant gym scene(s) and `PlayScene`; the repo duplicate-body guard and gym-parity assertions must pass unchanged. No behaviour/balance re-tuning (fire rates, beat grid, speeds, damage, ranges stay as-is).
- **Documentation updated.** README, the Game Design Document and any weapon/enemy design docs reflect the new per-weapon visuals and feel; new SFX cues are recorded in the audio cue manifest.
- **Full test suite passes** with the new changes, including updated graphics command-buffer tests and new per-weapon visual/audio tests.

## Constraints

- **Visuals only / no re-balance.** The epic must not change weapon behaviour (fire rates on the 80 BPM beat grid, bullet speed, lifetime/range, damage, patterns, counts). Only the rendered look, per-shot VFX and SFX change. Existing constants and the beat-grid invariant stay intact.
- **Code-drawn graphics.** All bullets remain Phaser `Graphics` primitives (no external sprite/texture assets), per the repo's neon code-drawn aesthetic.
- **Parity rule.** Shared behaviour lives once in `src/scenes/core/` + shared entities/utils; both the game (`PlayScene`) and gyms (`GymWeapons`, `GymFodderEnemies`, `GymBoss`, …) consume the same code. Divergence only with a documented reason in a work item and code comment.
- **Performance.** Bullet counts are high (Rapid 6/beat, Swarm bursts, Boss patterns). Per-shot VFX must stay cheap: small Graphics primitives, short lifetimes, reusing the existing `src/vfx/` patterns (bullet impact flash, split burst, aoe effect) rather than heavyweight effects.
- **Audio pipeline.** New SFX go through the baked ToneForge cue pipeline (`src/audio/effects.ts` + cue manifest), not procedural Web Audio; fire/impact cues for Wave Laser, Ricochet, Cluster and Options player weapons are currently missing and must be baked and added.
- **Ordering for implementation.** A shared bullet-shape rendering seam (used by `PlayerBullet` and `bulletUtils`) is the natural first child, since most weapon children depend on it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep.** Per-weapon polish can balloon into re-tuning unrelated systems. Any behaviour/balance change discovered while adding feel must be filed as a separate work item (link `related-to:AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE`), not absorbed into a weapon child.
- **Test churn in the shared visual seam.** Changing `PlayerBullet._draw` / `createBullet` will ripple through graphics command-buffer assertions and the duplicate-body parity guard; mitigation is a single shared data-driven seam and updating (not weakening) the affected tests.
- **Bot micro-simulation sensitivity.** Open item AH-0MV03PVZI009870X notes bot tests are sensitive to feel tweaks; coordinate if a child changes state exposed to `botSnapshot`.
- **Assumption — visuals only.** No weapon behaviour, fire rate, beat-grid, speed, lifetime, damage, pattern or count changes; only rendering, VFX and SFX. If a child needs the contrary, stop and re-plan.
- **Assumption — no new assets.** All new visuals are code-drawn Phaser `Graphics` primitives; no sprite sheets. New audio goes through the baked ToneForge cue pipeline.

## Existing state

- `PlayerBullet._draw()` (`src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`) renders **every** player bullet as a filled circle; the `bulletShape: 'line'` metadata on Dual and Wave Laser exists but is rendered as a scaled disc (documented in `weapons.ts`).
- All enemy bullets are created through `createBullet` (`src/entities/bulletUtils.ts`) — a filled circle per archetype, differentiated only by colour/size from `enemy-configs.csv`.
- Fire SFX already exist for cannon, spread, dual, rapid, nova, mortar, arc (`playWeaponFireSound` switch); **none** for wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options. No per-weapon impact sounds exist; enemy fire cues exist for scout, tank, phaser, diver, boss, swarm.
- VFX modules exist for bullet-vs-bullet impact, explosion particles, split burst, AOE effect, player death, wormhole spawn — but no per-weapon muzzle/trail/impact effects.
- Weapon HUD/drop **icons** were recently redesigned ("Symbols for weapons do not reflect what the weapon does", AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D) — that item covers pickup icons, this epic covers **in-flight projectiles**; keep the two distinct.

## Desired change

- Add a shared, data-driven bullet rendering seam so each weapon id (and each enemy archetype) resolves its own shape(s): disc for cannon/rapid, short line for dual, elongated beam for wave laser, teardrop/streak for ricochet, missile + flame for cluster, small pod shot for options, expanding ring for nova, arcing shell for mortar, jagged bolt for arc; enemy archetypes each get a distinctive geometry (e.g. Scout pellet, Diver shard, Tank shell, Phaser bolt, Swarm fleck, Raider dart, Boss pulse ring, Capturer beam, Orbital-Strike warhead).
- Add per-weapon spawn/muzzle VFX (light, cheap), optional trail, and distinct impact VFX + hit SFX through the shared combat-core spawn paths so game and gyms stay identical.
- Bake and wire the missing fire cues (wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options) and per-weapon impact cues; record them in the cue manifest.
- Extend the existing docs-guard test style with a weapon-visual roster test asserting each weapon/archetype resolves a unique visual signature.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — per-shape rendering (disc, line/beam, missile, shell, bolt) driven by weapon definition; keeps wrap/bounce/lifetime logic unchanged.
- `src/entities/bulletUtils.ts` — shared enemy-bullet creation; per-archetype shape seam used by every enemy class.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — extend `BulletShape`/`WeaponDefinition` with the visual metadata (per-shape parameters, trail, muzzle config) the seam consumes.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — carry new visual fields through level resolution without changing upgrade values.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` + `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` — new baked fire/impact cues (wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options; per-enemy impact cues); preserve the `playWeaponFireSound` single-path routing.
- `src/vfx/` — new per-weapon VFX modules (muzzle flash, trail, impact) following the existing `bulletImpact.ts`/`splitBurst.ts` conventions; reuse patterns where possible.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact hooks so game and gyms render identical feedback.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `GymFodderEnemies.ts`, `GymBoss.ts` — adopt the shared seams (parity).
- Enemy entities `src/entities/Scout.ts`, `Diver.ts`, `Tank.ts`, `Phaser.ts`, `Swarm.ts`, `Raider.ts`, `Boss.ts`, `Capturer.ts`, `OrbitalStrike.ts` — per-archetype bullet visuals/feel.
- Docs: `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (parity §5.1), audio cue documentation.

## Scope (planned child work items — one per weapon)

- **Player (11):** cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova, mortar, arc.
- **Enemy (12):** Scout/Invader aimed shot, Diver spread burst, Tank radial, Phaser radial, Swarm burst, Raider shot, Boss spread, Boss spiral, Boss pulse, Boss desperation, Capturer tractor beam, Orbital-Strike falling shell.

## Related work

- AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D — "Symbols for weapons do not reflect what the weapon does" (completed): weapon power-up **icons**; distinct scope from in-flight projectile graphics, but both aim at weapon legibility — keep aligned on per-weapon identity.
- AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4 — "New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games" (completed): research epic that added wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options; `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` records each concept's intended look.
- AH-0MV1BIUSJ0090W92 — "R-Type piercing wave laser" (completed): wave-laser **mechanics** (piercing); this epic adds its visual identity.
- AH-0MU43IIQV001S5JR — "When player shoots enemy bullet it should explode" (completed): shared bullet-vs-bullet impact flash; the per-weapon impact VFX should extend, not duplicate, this path.
- AH-0MV1BIVVK0043TEM — "Gradius Options orbiting satellites" (completed): pod visual already drawn in shared core; this epic gives pod shots their own feel.
- AH-0MV03PVZI009870X — "Make bot micro-simulation tests robust to small feel tweaks" (open): bot tests sensitive to feel tweaks; visual/SFX changes that alter snapshot-featured state may need coordination.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 — gym↔game parity convention (repository rule for every child).

### Automated find-related report

- AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J — "Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration tests" (completed): the weapon gym surfaces every player weapon — the natural place to watch each weapon's new feel.
- AH-0MUNS3ZQ1002DJ9S — "Advance waves on timer expiration" (completed): wave progression context for when enemy visuals change across waves.
- AH-0MUAYB5HR001HDYC — "Shields need to pulse and fade when ending" (completed): existing pulse/VFX precedent for the code-drawn effect style.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Enemy 'weapons': which enemy attacks get a child work item?" — Answer (operator): **A.** Every visually-distinct enemy attack producing a projectile or hazard: Scout/Invader aimed shot, Diver burst, Tank radial, Phaser radial, Swarm burst, Raider shot, Boss (all patterns), Capturer tractor beam, Orbital-Strike falling shell. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What counts as 'game feel' per weapon child?" — Answer (operator): **A, plus impact VFX/SFX.** Distinct in-flight bullet visuals **and** per-weapon VFX (muzzle flash/trail/impact) **and** per-weapon SFX cues for both fire and impact, mirrored identically in gyms and game. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "The Boss fires 4 distinct patterns (spread/spiral/pulse/desperation): one child or several?" — Answer (operator): **B.** One child per boss pattern (4 children). Source: interactive reply.

# Teleport and Phase Shift: Recharge System (AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR)

## Problem statement

Teleport and Phase Shift charges are consumed on use and never replenish, making them one-shot abilities. Both should recharge over a configurable period so charges return to a capped pool, with recharge time reduced at higher levels.

## Users

- **Primary player:** needs a safety net that recovers over time — a consumed escape should return rather than being gone forever.
- **Secondary player:** upgrade decisions should feel impactful; reduced recharge time is a meaningful progression incentive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Per-charge recharge model:** each consumed charge of Phase Shift and Teleport independently starts a recharge timer. When the timer elapses the charge returns to the pool. A consumed charge that has been recharged and spent again starts a new timer.
- **Maximum charge cap of 3:** the pool never exceeds 3 charges for either ability, whether collected (field pickup / hold-full reward) or recharged. Any collection or recharge that would exceed the cap is discarded.
- **Level-up reduces recharge time:** a new level variable `phaseRechargeTime` (seconds, exponential-saturation curve, e.g. base 30 s → cap 10 s) for Phase Shift and `teleportRechargeTime` (e.g. base 15 s → cap 5 s) — recharge time is level-derived. Higher levels = shorter recharge.
- **Permanent Phase Shift is a recharging pool:** the hold-full reward no longer grants unlimited activations; it adds one charge (up to the cap of 3) and recharges like any other charge.
- **HUD greys out unavailable items:** when a power-up has zero available charges, its HUD row (icon + label + value) is rendered greyed-out/inactive. When charges > 0 the row renders normally.
- **Field pickup grants one charge:** collecting Phase Shift or Teleport from the field grants one charge (level-derived via `phaseCharges` / `teleportStacks` from the level catalogue, clamped so total never exceeds 3).
- **All tests pass** with no build warnings — the full project test suite (`npm test`) and typecheck (`npm run typecheck`) both pass with the new changes.
- **Documentation updated** — the Game Design Document (teleport / phase-shift sections, power-up levelling section) and relevant code comments are updated to describe the recharge model; the CHANGELOG is managed by the ship skill's release pipeline and is excluded.

## Constraints

- Existing level curve infrastructure (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/utils/curve.ts`) must be reused — no new curve implementation.
- `PowerUpLevelStore` stack semantics must remain single-source-of-truth.
- Gym scenes must inherit the behaviour identically (gym ↔ game parity).
- PHASE_REARM_COOLDOWN (0.5 s shared governor for danger-triggered activations) remains unchanged.
- Recharge timers are run-scoped: they reset with the level store on run restart (weapon-parity, `PowerUpLevelStore.reset()`).
- Recharge timers tick while the game runs; no explicit pause-behaviour requirement (timers may pause with the scene — acceptable default, flagged for review).

## Existing state

- **Phase Shift** (`src/powerups/effects.ts`, `PowerUpLevelStore._phaseCharges`): stores a count of auto-activation charges. `consumePhaseCharge()` decrements; permanent grants `isPhasePermanent() === true` and bypasses the count.
- **Teleport** (`src/powerups/effects.ts`, `PowerUpLevelStore._teleportStacks`): stores FIFO uses. `consumeTeleport()` decrements.
- **Level catalogue** (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`): levels `phaseCharges` (1→3) and `teleportStacks` (1→3) via exponential-saturation curves. These represent *grant per pickup*, not pool size.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`): rows hidden when charge count = 0. Icons use `ICON_COLORS` (Phase Shift = grey `0xaaaaaa`, Teleport = orange).
- **No recharge mechanism exists.** Charges are consumed permanently.

## Desired change

- Replace the binary "has-charge / no-charge" model with a **per-charge recharge timer**.
- Introduce level variables for recharge time in the existing level catalogue.
- Apply the same cap-of-3 logic to both field-granted and permanently-granted charges.
- Grey-out HUD rows when the pool is empty.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — add `phaseRechargeTime`, `teleportRechargeTime` level specs; update `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — introduce per-charge recharge timers in `EffectsRegistry`; modify `consumePhaseCharge` / `consumeTeleport` to start timers.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — inject `PowerUpLevelStore` and tick recharge timers.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — detect zero-charges state and render greyed-out row.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — possibly add a grey-out variant for power-up icons.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.test.ts` / `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — recharge timer tests, cap-3 enforcement, level-derived recharge time, permanent Phase Shift as pool.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Balance risk:** the permanent Phase Shift reward is nerfed (unlimited → capped recharging pool). Mitigation: cap is deliberately 3 and recharge time is level-reducible; flagged for producer awareness.
- **Integration risk:** the shared automatic-defence resolver (`_updateAutoDefence`) selects between Phase Shift and Teleport based on available counts; with recharge, an empty pool contributes zero available count. Verify resolver ties/ordering still hold when both pools are partially charged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** related but out-of-scope opportunities (e.g. a visible recharge countdown bar, audio cues for recharge-complete, gym-specific recharge sliders) should be recorded as linked work items, not folded into this brief.
- **Assumption:** recharge time values (Phase 30 s → 10 s; Teleport 15 s → 5 s) are proposed defaults; exact base/cap/k are tunable during planning/implementation and must be re-confirmed if the producer prefers different pacing.

## Related work

- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — Power-up level curve catalogue (parent for all level variables).
- AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8 — Phase Shift automatic activation (parent for Phase Shift behaviour).
- AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC — Teleport automatic activation (parent for Teleport behaviour).
- AH-0MUX96GJF006CAZP — Enable mineral collection between waves.
- AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4 — Hold-full rewards in gyms.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should 'recharge' mean — per-charge cooldown, one shared cooldown, or other?" — Answer (producer): "(A) Per-charge cooldown — each consumed charge refills independently; a pool of N collected charges returns to N available. Recharge starts when a charge is spent." Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q: "Where is the 'upgrades list' that greys out?" — Answer (producer): "(A) HUD effect rows — the player's owned power-up list on the left stays visible but greys the row + icon while no charge is available." Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q: "Permanent Phase Shift interaction — keep unlimited, or make it a recharging pool?" — Answer (producer): "(B) It should be the ONLY recharge model. When picked up during play that is a single (stacking) charge. Once used it is gone. The recharges can stack too, up to a maximum of 3 (for both collected and recharged)." Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** – Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD (interactions, impacts, enemy actions, advanced telegraphing) (completed)
- **AH-0MUICQBE5007AIRU** – Add enemy-gym phase/shield gating regression tests (completed)
- **AH-0MV39AQOY006I083** – Update campaign documentation for 10-level structure (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muhmxwgc0058bo4, 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0mux96gjf006cazp, 0muze4aip009hzwc (+276 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0mux96gjf006cazp, 0muze4aip009hzwc, ability (+263 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muhmxwgc0058bo4, 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, 0mux96gjf006cazp, ability, add (+224 more)
## Plan (AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR)

Decomposed into **10 child features** (test/verification-first, dependency
ordered) plus **3 recorded out-of-scope follow-ups** (sibling items,
`discovered-from:AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR`).

1. **Unit tests: recharge-time level axes** (task, tests-first for #2) — verify
   `phaseRechargeRate` / `teleportRechargeRate` resolution, monotonicity, caps,
   time inverse (30→10 s / 15→5 s) and change-summary deltas. Files: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`.
2. **Recharge-time level axes in the power-up catalogue** (feature) — add the
   two rate axes (base→cap: Phase 1/30→1/10, Teleport 1/15→1/5 charges/s),
   stats/resolver exposure, seconds inverse, change summary; GDD §4.4
   levelling table row. Dep: #1. Files: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, GDD.
3. **Unit tests: per-charge recharge engine and cap-3** (task, tests-first for
   #4) — independent per-charge timers, cap-of-3 for collected/recharged,
   level-derived recharge time, permanent Phase Shift as pool, reset().
   Files: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`.
4. **Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore** (feature) — per-charge
   recharge timers + `tickRecharge(dt)`, cap-3 clamping on collect/recharge,
   `phaseRechargeTime()`/`teleportRechargeTime()`, permanent Phase Shift =
   recharging pool (+1 clamped), hold-full Teleport +1, run-scoped reset.
   Dep: #3. Files: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`.
5. **Tests: recharge tick, auto-defence resolver, scene parity** (task,
   tests-first for #6) — registry tick advances recharge, finite-pool
   `selectAutoDefence` (no Infinity), partial-pool tie/ordering, game↔gym
   parity through the shared tick path. Files: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`,
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
6. **Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence** (feature) —
   `EffectsRegistry.tick` advances store recharge timers; `selectAutoDefence`
   finite capped pools; empty pool contributes zero available count;
   PHASE_REARM_COOLDOWN unchanged. Dep: #5. Files: `src/powerups/effects.ts`.
7. **Tests: HUD grey-out for empty recharge pools** (task, tests-first for #8)
   — owned-but-empty Phase Shift/Teleport pool renders a greyed row; >0 renders
   normal; not-owned hidden; label counts recharge-aware. Files: `src/ui/HUD.test.ts`.
8. **HUD grey-out for zero-charge power-up rows** (feature) — greyed row
   (icon + label + value) when owned pool is empty; shared grey icon variant in
   `icons.ts`; row stays visible (not hidden). Dep: #7. Files: `src/ui/HUD.ts`,
   `src/powerups/icons.ts`.
9. **Document the recharge model (GDD + code comments)** (docs) — update GDD
   teleport/phase-shift sections, power-up levelling + HUD presentation, and
   module headers; no longer claim unlimited permanent activations. Dep: #8.
   Files: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`.
10. **Verify full suite + typecheck pass with recharge changes** (task,
    final gate for parent AC7) — `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` both pass;
    parity sweep green. Dep: #8, #9.

Test-first ordering guarantee: every implementation feature has its test item
created before it and dependency-wired (test → impl per feature; impl chain
#2→#4→#6→#8 carries the model forward).

## Plan Appendix (AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR)

- Q: "Recharge-time curve encoding — the brief's AC3 specifies a *decreasing*
  `phaseRechargeTime` (30 s → 10 s), but the shared exponential-saturation curve
  (`curveValue`) pins inverted specs flat at base, and the catalogue enforces a
  monotonic non-decreasing invariant (tests, parent AC4 of AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6).
  **Recommended:** (A) store increasing rates `phaseRechargeRate` /
  `teleportRechargeRate` (charges/s, Phase 1/30→1/10, Teleport 1/15→1/5) and
  expose the AC's seconds at point of use (`1/rate` → 30→10 s, 15→5 s),
  mirroring the `bombFrequency`/`bombInterval` precedent and reusing the curve
  with no new implementation." — Answer (operator): "1. A" (A). Final: A.
  Source: interactive reply, plan round 1.
- Q: "Field-pickup grant size — AC6 says field pickup "grants one charge"
  (level-derived via `phaseCharges`/`teleportStacks` from the catalogue,
  clamped ≤ 3). **Recommended:** (A) grant the level-derived count (1 at base
  level → up to 3), total clamped to 3, preserving the "grant per pickup"
  catalogue semantics described in the brief's Existing-state section." —
  Answer (operator): "2. A" (A). Final: A. Source: interactive reply, plan round 1.
- Q: "Teleport hold-full reward — the ACs redefine the Phase Shift permanent
  reward (permanent → +1 recharging charge ≤ 3) but are silent on the Teleport
  hold-full reward (today grants the level-derived stacks on a permanent grant).
  **Recommended:** (A) mirror Phase Shift — hold-full Teleport grants +1 charge
  (clamped ≤ 3) and recharges normally, keeping both defensive pools symmetric
  for the shared auto-defence resolver." — Answer (operator): "3. A" (A).
  Final: A. Source: interactive reply, plan round 1.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-14 (plan skill, Map): Q1–Q3 answered by the operator (A/A/A, plan

  reformatted from numbered (`1.`) to dash (`- `) bullets so the shared AC

  test-first dependency order (test items before their implementation items);
  3 out-of-scope follow-ups (recharge countdown bar, recharge-complete audio

# Centipede appears in the plain scenes column instead of ENEMIES (AH-0MV4ZOIZR0086T66)

## Problem statement

The dedicated `GymCentipede` enemy gym scene is discovered by the generic `Gym<Name>`
glob in `GymIndex` and rendered in the left-hand **plain scenes** column. The
Centipede is an enemy archetype, so it belongs in the middle **ENEMIES** column —
exactly where the analogous `GymBoss` scene already lives — so the index no longer
miscategorises an enemy testbed as a general-purpose scene.

## Users

- **Developer browsing the gym index** — expects enemy gym scenes to be grouped in the
  ENEMIES column so an enemy testbed is launched from the correct section.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want `GymCentipede` to appear in the **ENEMIES** column so that
  every enemy testbed is grouped together on the index.
- As a **developer**, I want `GymCentipede` to appear exactly once on the index (in the
  ENEMIES column, not the plain-scene column) so I don't see a confusing, miscategorised
  entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — `GymCentipede` removed from the plain scenes column:** `GymIndex.listedScenes`
      no longer contains `GymCentipede` and no `Centipede` text row is rendered at the
      plain-scenes column X (`GAME_WIDTH * GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X.scenes`).
- [ ] **AC2 — No separate `Centipede` entry on the gym index:** `GymIndex.listedEnemyScenes`
      contains exactly `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]` — no dedicated `Centipede` row — and
      `GymCentipede` is not listed in any index column (per the producer's review decision:
      "it should appear in the dropdown in the enemies gym", not as a separate entry).
- [ ] **AC3 — The `Centipede` enemy type appears in the in-panel dropdown of the enemies
      gym:** `GymFodderEnemies`'s enemy selector (`enemy-gym-select`) lists a `Centipede`
      option (label `Centipede`), alongside the discovered non-boss `EnemyConfig`s, and
      seeding `init({ enemyKey: 'centipede' })` works.
- [ ] **AC4 — Selecting `Centipede` in the enemies gym runs the shared linked chain:** the
      scene rebuilds via the *same* `CentipedeChain` / `Centipede` code `PlayScene` and
      `GymCentipede` run (`src/scenes/gym/core/centipedeFormation.ts`): one `Centipede`
      segment per `CENTIPEDE_SEGMENT_COUNT`, a shared chain, and the config-tuning controls
      hidden (the Centipede has no CSV row to tune or save). Switching back to a config
      archetype restores the config-driven formation and the tuning controls.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests:** `GymIndex.test.ts` drops the dedicated-row expectations; new
      assertions cover the dropdown `Centipede` option (presence, label, chain build,
      control hiding, round-trip back to a config). Every existing test continues to pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code
      comments, `README.md`, and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the three-column layout and the existing column X positions (`GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X`)
  unchanged; this is a categorisation change only.
- Mirror the existing `GymBoss` exclusion/surfacing pattern in `GymIndex.ts`; do **not**
  introduce a new generic "auto-route every enemy gym to ENEMIES" mechanism (scope creep —
  see Risks).
- No behavioural change to `GymCentipede` itself (only its index visibility/labelling).
- Do **not** modify `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` — it stays a pure discovery helper; the
  column categorisation is owned by `GymIndex`.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` builds `this.entries` from
  `discoverGymScenes(loadGymSceneModules())`, filtering out `GymFodderEnemies`, `GymBoss`
  and the Dev Utilities set (`DEV_UTILITY_SCENE_KEYS`). `GymCentipede` is **not** filtered,
  so it falls through into the left plain-scenes column.
- `this.enemyEntries` is currently hard-coded to `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCentipede.test.ts` asserts chain parity only; it does not assert index
  listing, so it needs no change.
- The Centipede is a **wave opt-in** (`centipede: true` in `PlayScene`), not a CSV enemy
  config, so it is not part of the `GymFodderEnemies` dropdown roster.

## Desired change (revised per producer review)

The producer's manual review (2026-10-14) rejected the dedicated-ENEMIES-row approach:
*"It appears in the enemies column now, but as a separate entry, it should appear in the
dropdown in the enemies gym."* The Centipede is an enemy archetype, so it should be
selectable **inside** the reusable enemies gym (`GymFodderEnemies`) rather than occupying a
separate index row (and it must stay out of the plain-scenes column).

1. Keep `GymCentipede` excluded from the plain-scenes list in `GymIndex.ts`.
2. Remove the dedicated `Centipede` ENEMIES row (`this.enemyEntries` reverts to
   `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]`).
3. Surface the Centipede as a dedicated option in `GymFodderEnemies`'s in-panel enemy
   selector (`enemy-gym-select`): selecting it (or deep-linking
   `init({ enemyKey: 'centipede' })`) swaps the scene to the **shared** centipede chain
   formation. The chain code is owned once in
   `src/scenes/gym/core/centipedeFormation.ts` and consumed by both `GymCentipede` and
   `GymFodderEnemies`, so game/gym parity holds by construction.
4. While the Centipede is active, hide the config-tuning controls (`#enemy-gym-config-body`):
   it is a wave opt-in, not a CSV row, so there is nothing to tune or save.
5. Update the module/class doc comments that enumerate the column exclusions, README and
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`. Do **not** modify `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`
   (pure discovery helper) or add a generic auto-route mechanism for every enemy scene.

## Key Files
## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/centipedeFormation.ts` — (new) the single shared Centipede chain
  formation config + per-scene chain registry, consumed by `GymCentipede` and
  `GymFodderEnemies`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCentipede.ts` — thin wrapper over the shared module (unchanged public
  API).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — add the `Centipede` option to the enemy selector;
  branch `init`/`_selectEnemy` to the shared centipede formation; hide `#enemy-gym-config-body`
  while the Centipede is active.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — keep `GymCentipede` excluded from the plain scenes; remove the
  dedicated ENEMIES row; update column doc comments.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — updated and
  new assertions as per AC5.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §Gym surface / §8.5: record that the Centipede
  is surfaced in the enemies-gym dropdown, excluded from the plain scene list and not a
  separate ENEMIES row.
- `README.md` — §Gym Index Entry Scene: ENEMIES column roster is `Fodder Enemies`, `Boss`;
  the Centipede lives in the fodder gym's dropdown.

## Related work
## Related work

- **Boss appears in both lists on index screen (AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X)** — established the
  precedent: exclude an enemy scene from the plain-scene column and surface a dedicated
  ENEMIES row that boots the scene directly.
- **Single enemy gym scene with in-panel enemy selector dropdown (AH-0MV13G5EV008D41E)** —
  defines the three-column index layout and the ENEMIES column semantics.
- **Centipede segmented chain (AH-0MV01EJ92008ZZ86)** — created the `GymCentipede` scene.
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** —
  sibling categorisation pattern (Dev Utilities column owns tooling scenes).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCNZ7DN0049K73** – Scene-level tests: GymPowerUps via gameHarness (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)
- **AH-0MV2XDEKN0031KX4** – Test: gym parity intact (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: archetype, centipede, column, gym, scene (+34 more)
- `README.md` — matched: appears, archetype, centipede, column, enemies (+33 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: appears, archetype, centipede, column, currently (+30 more)

Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MV4ZOIZR0086T66.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (revised by producer review):** "should be an enemy" means the Centipede
  should be reachable **inside** the enemies gym — surfaced as a dedicated **option in the
  `GymFodderEnemies` in-panel enemy selector**, which boots the same shared linked-chain code
  — rather than as a separate index entry *or* a CSV fodder config (the Centipede is a wave
  opt-in, not a CSV row). The producer rejected the dedicated ENEMIES row in review
  (2026-10-14).
- **Risk: Low.** A categorisation + dropdown-surface change with shared-code extraction; no
  gameplay, entity or spawn behaviour changes. The dedicated `GymCentipede` scene is
  unchanged in behaviour and keeps its parity tests.
- **Failure mode:** a `Centipede` label present on the index at all would make the
  `findTextAt` label lookups ambiguous — resolved by keeping `GymCentipede` out of every
  index column; it is only reachable through the fodder gym's dropdown.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general "auto-route every enemy gym scene to the ENEMIES column"
  mechanism is out of scope here; if wanted it should be captured as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No clarifying questions were required.** Research summary: the seed intent, combined
  with the existing `GymBoss` precedent (AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X) and the documented three-column
  index contract (`src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §"Gym surface", `README.md` §"Gym Index Entry Scene"), was sufficient to draft a clear
  brief. The one interpretation choice (dedicated ENEMIES **scene** row that boots
  `GymCentipede` directly, rather than adding a fodder-dropdown config) is recorded as an
  explicit documented assumption under Risks & assumptions.

# Orbital Fires in direction of orb

## Headline

Make the Gradius Options escort pods fire each bullet **radially outward along the pod's own orbit direction** (away from the ship, through the pod's current position) instead of along the ship's heading, keeping the synchronized beat-grid volley and guaranteeing the orbit never lines up with the fire cadence so consecutive volleys aim differently.

## Problem statement

Today the two (up to six) orbiting satellite pods of the Options weapon each fire a bullet **along the ship's heading** (`optionsPodFireDirections` returns the ship's heading for every pod). The operator wants the escort to feel like a spread of independent emitters: each pod should fire **in whatever direction the pod itself is pointing at the moment of firing** — i.e. radially away from the ship through the pod's orbit angle. Because the pods orbit, this turns each volley into a rotating spike pattern that fans in different directions over time. Care is needed so the orbit speed does not complete a whole number of revolutions per fire trigger, which would make every volley aim identically.

## Users / user stories

**User story (player):** As a player using the Options escort, I want each orbiting pod to shoot outward along its own orbit direction rather than copying the ship's facing, so that building the escort sprays fire in a rotating spread that covers more of the arena.

**User story (operator/designer):** As a designer, I want the orbit rotation speed to avoid completing exactly one (or a whole number of) revolution(s) between consecutive fire triggers, so that consecutive volleys always aim in different directions and the spread feels alive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Radial fire direction:** Each pod fires its bullet radially outward from the ship through the pod's current orbit position: the bullet's velocity angle equals the pod's orbit angle (`positions[i].angle`) at fire time, not the ship's heading. Verified by unit tests on the shared `optionsPodFireDirections` helper and an updated scene test asserting each pod bullet's `atan2(vy, vx)` angle equals its orbit angle at the pod bullet speed.
- **AC2 — Synchronized beat-grid volley:** Pods still fire as one synchronized volley on the shared 80 BPM beat grid at the Options subdivision (1 shot/beat, 750 ms at default BPM). The fire cadence, phase-locking and `isOnBeatGrid` catalogue invariant are unchanged; existing beat-grid tests stay green.
- **AC3 — Non-aligned orbit vs trigger:** The orbit period (`OPTIONS_ORBIT_PERIOD_MS` = 2000 ms) is not a whole-number multiple of the Options fire interval (750 ms at default BPM) — i.e. revolutions-per-trigger is non-integer — and a pure helper plus unit test asserts this. A test also verifies that two consecutive volleys produce **different** fire-direction sets while every single volley still aims radially.
- **AC4 — Gym↔game parity:** The radial fire direction lives once in the shared `optionsEscort` seam consumed by `CombatCoreScene.fireOptionsPods` and the gyms; the Options orbit-emitter parity block in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` stays green (a divergent gym copy would trip the repo-wide duplicate-body guard).
- **AC5 — Documentation updated:** The `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.options.description`, `src/utils/weapons.ts` header notes, `src/scenes/core/optionsEscort.ts` module/JSDoc comments, the README P-weapons catalogue line, docs/Game Design Document.md (P6 row and the §Options implementation note) and docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md Gradius Options section all describe pods firing radially outward (in the direction of the orb), not along the heading.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation:** At least one new or updated automated test covers the radial firing behaviour for multiple pod counts and a range of orbit phases (including a custom radius), and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Beat-grid invariant:** All fire rates remain exact subdivisions of the configurable 80 BPM beat (`isOnBeatGrid`); the Options weapon stays at subdivision 1 (one synchronized volley per beat). No new `AoEDescriptor`.
- **Gym↔game parity:** All gameplay behaviour lives in the shared core (`optionsEscort.ts` + `CombatCoreScene.fireOptionsPods`); the game and every gym run identical code with no divergent copies.
- **Orbit tuning (operator decision Q3A):** Keep the fixed `OPTIONS_ORBIT_PERIOD_MS = 2000` orbit period; do not re-tune it. Enforce the non-alignment (rev-per-trigger ≠ whole number) with a test/invariant.
- **Pods remain decorative satellites:** they never block bullets and never collide; only their fire direction changes.
- **Determinism & purity:** Fire-direction geometry stays in the pure, side-effect-free helper; no Phaser/global access; deterministic for a given `(phase, count)`.
- Written in UK English.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/core/optionsEscort.ts` — pure shared seam: `optionsPodPositions` returns each pod's `{x, y, angle}` on the orbit; `optionsPodFireDirections(heading, count)` returns `[heading, heading, …]` (every pod fires along the ship's heading).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` (`fireOptionsPods`, ~line 952) — computes pod positions from `this._optionsOrbitPhase` and `directions = optionsPodFireDirections(player.getHeading(), count)`, then spawns one `PlayerBullet` per pod at the pod's position with that direction.
- Subdivision/period facts: `WEAPON_OPTIONS_SUBDIVISION = 1` → `WEAPON_OPTIONS_FIRE_RATE = 750 ms` at 80 BPM; `OPTIONS_ORBIT_PERIOD_MS = 2000`; 750/2000 = 0.375 rev/trigger (non-integer, so directions already vary across volleys today).
- Tests that encode the heading-direction behaviour and will need updating: `src/scenes/core/optionsEscort.test.ts` (fire-directions describe), `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` (~line 1448 "each pod fires along the heading"), and the parity lifetimes in `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **Fire direction:** Each pod's bullet flies radially outward from the ship through the pod's current orbit angle. The shared `optionsPodFireDirections` helper changes signature/behaviour to return, for each pod, its radial direction (equivalently its orbit `angle`) derived from the orbit phase and pod index — no longer the ship's heading. `CombatCoreScene.fireOptionsPods` consumes the per-pod directions (e.g. from `positions[i].angle`) instead of `player.getHeading()`.
2. **Volley cadence unchanged:** All pods still fire together once per beat at subdivision 1 (synchronized, phase-locked volley on the shared beat clock).
3. **Non-alignment guarantee:** Add a small pure helper exposing revolutions-per-trigger (`fireIntervalMs / OPTIONS_ORBIT_PERIOD_MS`) and a unit test asserting it is non-integer for the Options fire cadence; add a test that two consecutive volleys (advanced orbit phase between triggers) aim in different directions.
4. **Docs & catalogue text:** update every description of the Options weapon to say pods fire radially outward in the direction of the orb at fire time.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/optionsEscort.ts` — Change `optionsPodFireDirections` to derive each pod's radial-outward direction from its orbit angle; update module/JSDoc; add the revolutions-per-trigger helper.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `fireOptionsPods` uses per-pod radial directions instead of `player.getHeading()`; update inline comments.
- `src/scenes/core/optionsEscort.test.ts` — Update fire-direction tests to assert radial angles; add revolutions-per-trigger and consecutive-volley-variation tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — Update the pod-bullet direction assertion (~line 1448) from heading to radial (orbit angle).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — Review the Options orbit-emitter parity block; adjust only if it encodes heading-direction assertions.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.options.description` and header note ("fire along the ship's heading" → radial outward).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` / `GymWeapons.test.ts` — Exercised only; verify no heading-direction assumptions for the Options weapon.
- `README.md` — P-weapons catalogue line for `options` (line ~809).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — P6 weapons table row and the §Options implementation note (~lines 606, 637).
- `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` — Gradius Options section (~lines 230–273).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "radial outward" = the direction from the ship centre through the pod's position (`positions[i].angle`); this matches the operator's Q1 answer (spike/flower pattern).
- **Assumption:** pod count, orbit radius, pod size and bullet speed are unchanged; only the fire direction changes. Any balance re-tuning is out of scope.
- **Risk:** other tests or gym scenes may encode the heading-firing behaviour beyond the ones listed under Key Files; a full-suite pass is the gate, and any newly discovered heading-direction assertions must be updated with the same change.
- **Risk (visual/balance):** radial firing weakens straight-line damage ahead of the ship (the original Gradius-trail identity). This is the requested design change; no mitigation requested.
- **Scope-creep risk:** suggested enhancements such as per-pod staggered fire, homing pod shots (the planned `homing` upgrade noted in the research doc) or orbit-speed re-tuning are **out of scope** and must be raised as new work items, not folded in here.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1BIVVK0043TEM — Gradius Options orbiting satellites (completed):** the parent design/implementation this item refines; ships the shared `optionsEscort` seam and the current heading-firing behaviour. This item is a follow-up change to that behaviour.
- **AH-0MTECNKPC00954HH — Test: Per-scene — player/combat assertions + regression (completed):** regression coverage that includes Options; should stay green.
- **AH-0MV822G6F002JRRY — Capturer tractor beam projectile identity (blocked):** unrelated (capturer beam), listed by the automated find-related report for `fire`/`direction` keyword overlap only.
- **AH-0MV1BIW95004POSX — Pac-Man power pellet fright (completed):** unrelated; automated-report keyword overlap only.
- Automation: find-related report persisted in `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MV5DFBVW002J2XO.md`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: What does "direction of the orb" mean for the fired bullet?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **A — Radially outward from the ship** (bullet travels along the line from ship → pod, a rotating spike/flower pattern). Recommended option accepted. Research: `PodPosition.angle` already encodes the ship→pod direction (`optionsPodPositions`), so radial-outward is exactly `positions[i].angle`.
- **Q2: Should pods still fire as one synchronized volley on the 80 BPM beat grid?** — Answer (operator): **A — Yes**, all pods fire together at subdivision 1, phase-locked as today. Recommended option accepted. Research: `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` fires all pods on the Options beat tick via `fireOptionsPods`; cadence lives in `WEAPON_OPTIONS_SUBDIVISION`.
- **Q3: How should the "rotation ≠ 1 revolution per trigger" constraint be enforced?** — Answer (operator): **A — Keep the fixed 2000 ms orbit speed and add an invariant test guaranteeing revolutions-per-trigger is never a whole number.** Recommended option accepted. Research: current 750 ms trigger / 2000 ms orbit = 0.375 rev/trigger (already non-integer); the guarantee should cover the configurable subdivision/BPM and be documented.

# Asteroids drop more lives — intake brief

## Problem statement

Fully destroyed (terminal **small-tier**) asteroids deserve a meaningful recovery reward: today a small asteroid kill only rolls the shared 18% generic drop pool and drops a single mineral, so it never guarantees a shot at the rare (≈ 7.5 % of power-up draws) **Extra Life**. This change gives every small asteroid a small, configurable chance to drop an Extra Life power-up in addition to its existing rolls, so smashing rocks down a split chain offers a real recovery path toward the 5-life cap.

## Users and user stories

- **As a player**, I want a small asteroid I fully destroy to occasionally drop an **Extra Life** power-up, so clearing the asteroid field gives me a recovery opportunity, not just minerals.
- **As a game designer**, I want the extra-life chance to be tunable in one persisted place, so I can dial the generosity of asteroid drops without touching per-scene code.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the game and every asteroid-bearing gym to run the same drop rule, so the gym↔game parity guard holds and the two cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Roll scope:** Only a **small** asteroid that is fully destroyed rolls the Extra Life drop. Large/medium asteroids (which split instead) never roll it, and non-asteroid enemies are unaffected. Verified by unit tests over the shared rule and by `PlayScene`/gym kill-path tests.
2. **Chance + configurability:** A fully destroyed small asteroid rolls an Extra Life drop with probability `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`, default **0.05**, held on `GameRules` and persisted/loaded through `src/core/rules.ts` (clamped to `[0, 1]`); an older persisted rules blob without the key loads the default without migration.
3. **Drop composition:** When the roll succeeds, exactly one **Extra Life** (`extra_life`) power-up drop is spawned at the asteroid's death site with the standard drop placement (separation nudging); the 5% roll is **additional** to — not instead of — the existing generic per-kill drop roll (asteroids stay in the shared weighted pool) and to the existing mineral drop rule (small → 1 mineral, large/medium → none), which are unchanged.
4. **Gym↔game parity:** The Extra Life roll is implemented once as a shared rule in `src/scenes/core/` (registered in the repo-wide duplicate-body guard) and consumed by `PlayScene` and the asteroid-bearing gyms (`GymMinerals`, `GymFodderEnemies` asteroid row, `GymLevel`), so no scene re-implements it.
5. **Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover the shared rule (tier gating, chance math with injected RNG, boundary values) and scene tests assert that a seeded small-asteroid kill with the roll set to 1.0 spawns an `extra_life` drop while large/medium kills never do; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` parity block registers the shared helper.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.1 E6, §4.4) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Asteroids remain in the shared weighted-random drop pool: the generic per-kill roll (18%, `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE`) is **unchanged** for asteroids (operator Q2 answer — the description was adjusted to match).
- No new power-up type; reuse the existing `extra_life` pickup (`EXTRA_LIFE_DROP_ID`), its icon and its collect path (`PlayScene.onPowerUpCollected` / shared drop layer).
- Large/medium asteroids may continue to award no score and roll no Extra Life (they split, unchanged).
- Gym cadence-based drop sourcing (OQ6 divergence) is unchanged; the per-kill Extra Life roll is a separate, additional seam.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` (≈ L2760) calls `_maybeDropPowerUp(x, y)` for **every** kill — asteroids included — rolling `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE = 0.18` against the shared `WeightedRandomSpawner` (`src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`) built from `rules.powerUpWeights`/`rules.weaponWeights`; all power-ups and weapons are possible asteroid drops today.
- Minerals: the shared rule `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` drops one mineral for small asteroids, none for large/medium; unchanged.
- Asteroid splitting: `src/scenes/core/asteroidSplit.ts`; a destroyed large/medium just spawns two children (no kill-drop for the parent), and a small asteroid destroys cleanly (terminal).
- `GameRules` (`src/core/rules.ts`, `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION = 4`) persists tunables in localStorage with defaults-merge; new keys default without a version bump.
- Gyms: `GymFormationScene.onEnemyDestroyed` (kill path) and `GymLevel.onEnemyDestroyed` consume the shared mineral rule; `GymFodderEnemies`/`GymBoss` enable the opt-in cadence power-up layer (`powerUps: {}`), `GymMinerals` does not.
- GDD §4.1 E6 documents asteroid tiers/splitting; §4.4 documents drop weights; `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 mandates shared-code parity.

## Desired change

Add a configurable `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` (default 0.05) rule. In the shared `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts` pure helper, `rollAsteroidExtraLife(entity, rng, chance)` returns true only when the entity is a small asteroid and `rng() < chance`. `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` and the gym kill paths call it after the generic drop roll and spawn one `extra_life` drop when it returns true (placement nudging reused; no generic-pool draw). Gyms opt in so parity is observable and provable.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/rules.ts` — add `GameRules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`, `DEFAULT_ASTEROID_EXTRA_LIFE_DROP_CHANCE = 0.05`, wire into `DEFAULT_RULES`, `cloneDefaultRules()` and `loadRules()` (coerce + clamp `[0,1]`).
- `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts` (new) — shared pure rule `rollAsteroidExtraLife` (tier gate + chance roll).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_onEnemyKilled`: after `_maybeDropPowerUp`, roll the shared rule for asteroids and `spawnPowerUpDrop('extra_life', x, y)`; cache the chance from `loadRules()`.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `onEnemyDestroyed`/`_dropMineralsForKill` path: apply the shared rule and spawn via the drop seam.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — enable the per-kill Extra Life drop path (asteroids-only gym demonstrates the behaviour).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — consume the shared rule in their kill paths (asteroid row/asteroid spawns).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — register `rollAsteroidExtraLife` in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` so the duplicate-body guard covers it.
- Tests (new/updated): `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.test.ts`; `PlayScene.test.ts`; `GymMinerals.test.ts`; `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts`; `GymLevel.test.ts`; `src/core/rules.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.1 E6, §4.4), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§5.1 + asteroid sections), README if it documents drop behaviour, CHANGELOG excluded (ship skill).

## Related work

- Increase the probability of lives powerup being spawned (AH-0MUNS3VAQ0023L1J) — Extra Life weight 1 → 3 (background; unchanged by this item).
- Add an extra life power up (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3); Power-up catalogue + effects (AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS).
- Asteroids as an enemy (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F); AsteroidSpawner (AH-0MUGCH1L0005HXDG); asteroids not wave-accounted (AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO); minerals/hold (AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q).
- Shared mineral kill-drop rule (AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB) — template for the new shared rule.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Economy creep:** more frequent Extra Life pickups risk runs grinding to max lives. Mitigation: 5% is deliberately small, only terminal small kills, and the existing 5-life cap bounds the effect.
- **Roll double-dip:** a small asteroid already rolls the generic pool; the 5% roll is additive by design (operator Q2b). Monitor whether small-asteroid kills become noticeably "rich". Recorded as a tunable so it is reversible in one place.
- **Gym wiring scope:** enabling a per-kill drop path in gyms that currently use cadence sourcing is the largest touch-surface; keep the cadence layer untouched and add the per-kill seam as a separate opt-in path to avoid disturbing gym behaviour/tests.
- **Assumption (Q3, gym half):** operator chose the `GameRules`-field option; gym consumption of the shared rule is assumed required by the repo parity convention (recorded in the interview appendix; flag if unintended).
- **No schema bump:** new optional key merges over defaults; no migration needed (verify in tests).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When does the 5% extra-life roll fire — only the terminal small tier (a), any asteroid kill (b), any kill incl. split children (c)?" — Answer (operator): **A** — only fully destroyed (small) asteroids; large/medium split and roll nothing. Source: interactive reply (comment AH-C0MV82SOQP00292FQ).
- Q2: "Should the 5% roll replace the generic 18% per-kill pool for asteroids, or be additive?" — Answer (operator): **B — additive**; asteroids keep the generic pool (they may still drop other power-ups/weapons) and the 5% Extra Life roll is additional for small asteroids; description updated to match. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Where should the 5% be configured?" — Answer (operator): **A** — a `GameRules` field `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` (default 0.05), persisted via `rules.ts`; gym consumption of the shared rule assumed per gym↔game parity convention (second half of the recommended option; treated as required unless the producer objects). Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA** – Mineral rules tunables and per-enemy mineral count (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (completed)
- **AH-0MUTYV7SQ005HURT** – Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: additional, asteroid, asteroids, bearing, cannot (+58 more)
- `README.md` — matched: additional, asteroid, asteroids, bearing, cannot (+57 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: additional, asteroid, asteroids, bearing, cannot (+57 more)

# Reduce the volume of shots for Tank and Scout — Intake Brief

> Halve the effective playback volume of the Tank and Scout enemy **fire
> sequence** — both the advance (warmup) whine/blip cues and the shot cues
> (`playTankAdvanceCue`/`playTankFireSound`, `playScoutAdvanceCue`/
> `playScoutFireSound`) — via a single named 0.5 gain at the shared audio seam.

> **Producer clarification (intake Q2 answer = "yes" + audit rejection of the
> first pass):** the advance/warmup cues ARE part of the reduction. First pass
> (commit 1dd37a92) halved only the shot cues and was rejected: "Still too
> loud, perhaps because the warmup sounds were not reduced?" 

## Problem Statement

The Tank (E3) and Scout (E1) enemy **shot** cues — `playTankFireSound` and
`playScoutFireSound` — currently play at full volume (default gain 1.0) and sit
too loud in the mix. Both shot cues must play at **half their current volume**
(linear gain × 0.5) so enemy fire reads clearly without overpowering the rest
of the game audio.

## Users

- The player, hearing enemy fire alongside player weapon cues, pickups, and
  destruction sounds.

## User Stories

- As a player, I hear the Tank cannon thump and the Scout laser shot at roughly
  half their current loudness, so enemy fire no longer dominates the audio mix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Tank fire sequence at half volume:** `playTankAdvanceCue()` and
  `playTankFireSound()` play the baked `aihell-tank-advance` / `aihell-tank-fire`
  assets at an effective gain of exactly `0.5` (previous default 1.0) — verified
  via the recording-provider assertion (`recording.plays[].volume === 0.5`). The
  advance-cue no-gap delay (`TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION`) is preserved.
- **AC2 — Scout fire sequence at half volume:** `playScoutAdvanceCue()` and
  `playScoutFireSound()` play the baked `aihell-scout-advance` /
  `weapon-laser-zap` assets at an effective gain of exactly `0.5` — verified via
  the recording-provider assertion. The advance-cue no-gap delay
  (`SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION`) is preserved.
- **AC3 — Named tunable, nothing else changes:** the 0.5 gain is exposed as a
  single named constant (`TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`) so it is tunable in
  one place; it applies to the four Tank/Scout fire-sequence cues and every
  other cue's volume is unchanged (no collateral volume changes — the Phaser
  cues and all other enemies keep their volumes). Note: `playScoutAdvanceCue`
  is also consumed by `OrbitalStrike` (its telegraph tell) — that shared-cue
  reuse inherits the halved volume, which is consistent with the quieter-mix
  intent.
- **AC4 — Tests + full suite:** `src/audio/effects.test.ts` asserts the halved
  volumes for all four fire-sequence cues (and the existing advance→fire
  no-gap timing still holds); entity tests in `src/entities/Tank.test.ts` /
  `src/entities/Scout.test.ts` remain green. **Full project test suite must
  pass with the new changes.**
- **AC5 — Documentation updated:** all related documentation is updated to
  reflect the change — GDD §7.3 (SFX Event Catalog "Enemy actions" entry and
  the Per-Enemy Audio Character tank/scout descriptions), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (note the 0.5× runtime volume trim on
  the `playTankFireSound` / `playScoutFireSound` rows).

## Constraints

- 50% reduction only — linear gain × 0.5, matching the thruster-volume
  precedent (AH-0MUAYB8S50029QB8 halved `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME`).
- Implemented as a playback-time volume option through the existing `playCue`
  seam — **no WAV re-baking**, no recipe changes, no other audio parameters
  altered.
- The change lives in `src/audio/effects.ts`, the single shared audio seam, so
  game ↔ gym parity is automatic (Tank/Scout entity code is shared).

## Existing State

- `src/audio/effects.ts`:
  - `playTankFireSound()` → `playCue('playTankFireSound', { delay: TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION })` — volume default 1.0. Asset: `aihell-tank-fire` (seed 32141, baked), consumer `src/entities/Tank.ts` (`tryFireRadialBurst`).
  - `playScoutFireSound()` → `playCue('playScoutFireSound', { delay: SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION })` — volume default 1.0. Asset: `weapon-laser-zap` (existing recipe, default seed 1), consumer `src/entities/Scout.ts` (aimed shot) + `src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts` (reuses only `playScoutAdvanceCue`, not the fire sound).
- Neither baked asset is shared by any other cue, so scaling these two plays
  cannot affect any other sound.
- Existing tests (`effects.test.ts`, `Tank.test.ts`, `Scout.test.ts`) assert
  invocation counts and the no-gap advance→fire delay; none assert volume for
  these cues, so no existing assertion needs to be rewritten (new ones added).

## Desired Change

- In `src/audio/effects.ts`, expose a single named constant
  (`TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE = 0.5`) and pass `volume:
  TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` in all four Tank/Scout fire-sequence cues
  (`playTankAdvanceCue`, `playTankFireSound`, `playScoutAdvanceCue`,
  `playScoutFireSound`) — alongside the existing `delay` where present.
- Update the two docs listed in AC5.
- Add recording-provider volume assertions to `effects.test.ts`.

## Key Files

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — apply `volume: 0.5` (named constant) to the Tank/Scout fire cue options
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — assert `playTankFireSound()` / `playScoutFireSound()` play at volume 0.5; keep no-gap delay assertions
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 SFX Event Catalog + Per-Enemy Audio Character (Tank/Scout)
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — note the 0.5× runtime trim on the two fire rows
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §6 Audio Best Practices / per-enemy audio (only if fire-sound volume is stated)

## Related Work

- **AH-0MUAYB8S50029QB8** — Reduce Volume of Player Thrusters (precedent: "reduce volume by 50%" = halve the gain)
- **AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU** — Remove the gap between Scout advance cue and shot (advance→fire no-gap contract these cues must keep)
- **AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE** — Tank has no audio (original Tank audio work)
- **AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19** — Scout has no audio (original Scout audio work)
- **AH-0MUTYV92Y000WJ8Z** — Rewrite effects.ts to Phaser playback (ToneForge migration — current playback layer)
- **AH-0MUA8B6MT006M1KS** — SFX master volume + mute plumbing in effects.ts

## Risks & Assumptions

- **"Half the volume" is linear gain × 0.5** (not a perceptual −10 dB re-bake),
  matching the thruster-volume precedent. Baked assets have no noise floor, so
  a simple gain trim is clean.
- **Scope covers the whole Tank/Scout fire sequence** — advance whines/blips
  AND shot cues are halved (producer Q2 answer "yes"; audit rejection "warmup
  sounds were not reduced"). The Phaser fire sequence and every other cue stay
  at full volume.
- **Runtime gain, not WAV re-bake** — keeps the change minimal and the
  amplitude documented in the assets intact; the master SFX gain still applies
  on top.
- **Scope-creep risk:** other enemy shot volumes, music/sfx re-balancing, or
  re-baking assets are out of scope — track as `discovered-from:AH-0MV74ROYR009X8U3`
  work items if requested.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 — "Half the volume": linear 50% gain, or perceptual loudness halving?
  — Answer (operator directive + precedent): linear gain × 0.5. Research:
  the thruster-volume item (AH-0MUAYB8S50029QB8) treated "reduce by 50%" as
  halving the gain constant (0.15 → 0.075) with no perceptual caveats.
- Q2 — Does "shots" include the advance whines/blips? — Answer (assumption,
  item wording): no — only `playTankFireSound` / `playScoutFireSound`; the
  advance cues are telegraphs. Recorded as an assumption in Risks & Assumptions.

  **Answer (producer):** yes- Q3 — Re-bake the baked WAVs at half amplitude vs. runtime gain?

# Ship shape needs to point in the direction of travel

## Problem statement

Give the player ship a forward cue: the Asteroids hull's rear edge becomes
concave so the silhouette points along the direction of travel. Scope is the
Asteroids scheme only — the four-directional scheme keeps its invariant
hexagon.

## Users

- **Players** — need an immediate read on which way the ship is facing at all
  times, especially while turning and thrusting in the Asteroids scheme.
- **AI agents / developers** — need a deterministic, geometry-based change that
  keeps `shipSize` semantics, config wiring, physics, and engine-port layout
  intact so existing behaviour and tests carry over.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want the hull silhouette to show a forward direction, so I
  can tell at a glance which way the ship will travel when I thrust.
- As a **player**, I want the cue to stay subtle and consistent with the neon
  geometric palette, so it reads as a ship, not a cartoon arrow.
- As a **developer**, I want the four-directional scheme's invariant hexagon
  untouched, so that scheme's cardinal engine ports and directionless look are
  preserved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Concave rear edge (Asteroids only):** In the `asteroids` control
  scheme the player hull keeps the hexagon form but its **rear edge** (the side
  opposite the nose, -x in the ship's local frame) is **concave** — a shallow
  inward notch — so the silhouette has a clear forward direction that aligns
  with the ship's facing. The `fourDirectional` scheme keeps the current
  invariant regular hexagon (no notch).
- [ ] **AC2 — Facing alignment & rotation:** The forward cue points along the
  ship's facing: the whole hull (body + concave rear + engine ports) continues
  to rotate with the Graphics object in the Asteroids scheme, so the ship
  visibly points in the direction of travel while turning and thrusting.
  Stationary behaviour holds the **most recent heading** (no snap to a default).
- [ ] **AC3 — Geometry & physics preserved:** The hull's bounding
  circumradius still equals `shipSize / 2` (the notch is an inward cut that must
  not expand the bounding circle); engine port positions (main rear,
  forward-side, nose retro-thruster) stay in the same local frame; no changes to
  `utils/movementModel.ts` physics, input mapping, or firing logic.
- [ ] **AC4 — Config wiring preserved:** Rendering remains driven by
  `ShipConfig` (`shipColor`, `shipSize`, thrust-flame colours/lengths) and works
  with live `setConfig` and the gym sliders. No new config keys.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests:** Existing four-directional hull tests (6-edge invariant
  hexagon, ports, flames) remain green and unchanged in intent; a new Asteroids
  hull test asserts the concave rear (e.g. an extra interior vertex on the -x
  side / non-straight rear edge) and that the Asteroids silhouette is **not**
  rotationally invariant. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 player-hull
  description is amended to describe the Asteroids concave-rear hull (and the
  divergence from the four-directional invariant hexagon); code comments in
  `src/entities/Player.ts` are updated to match.

## Constraints

- Follow GDD §7.2 visual style: geometric/angular silhouettes, neon outline
  (lineStyle 2, `shipColor`, alpha 1), **no fill**; the concave cue must stay
  within the geometric palette (not an organic/curvy shape).
- This deliberately reverses part of the earlier direction-neutral decision
  (AH-0MTBOIIF6004GPY8 / AH-0MTAF76Q1008BLBE): the reversal is scoped to the
  **Asteroids** scheme only; the four-directional scheme keeps the invariant
  hexagon. The GDD must document this scheme divergence.
- `shipSize` keeps its existing meaning (half-size / circumradius used by
  physics-adjacent callers); no physics or input changes.
- Change lives once in the shared `src/entities/Player.ts` so game and gyms
  cannot diverge (gym↔game parity — the player entity is instantiated by
  `PlayScene` and every gym).

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Player.ts` `_redraw()` draws a regular hexagon (flat
  top/bottom, vertices at angles 0°/60°/…/300°, circumradius `shipSize / 2`,
  stroke-only neon) for **both** schemes; the entire Graphics object rotates by
  the facing angle in the Asteroids scheme (`setRotation(facing)`), so the
  hexagon looks identical before and after rotation — no forward cue.
- Engine ports: `FOUR_DIR_ENGINES` (top/bottom/left/right cardinals, size 1)
  and `ASTEROIDS_ENGINES` (main rear at -x, two 70% forward-side at +x, nose
  retro-thruster at +x) drawn as quarter-circle arcs on the hull.
- Tests in `src/entities/Player.test.ts` assert the invariant hexagon
  (6 edge segments, all vertices on the circumradius circle) using the
  four-directional config; gear that keeps asserting the invariant shape is
  shared with the Asteroids-path body test.
- Default `controlScheme` is now `asteroids` (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`).

## Desired change

- In `_redraw()`, when the active scheme is `asteroids`, draw the hull as the
  regular hexagon **with a concave rear edge**: replace the straight -x edge
  (between the two rear vertices) with a shallow inward V-notch (one
  additional interior vertex along the -x side), keeping all other vertices on
  the circumradius circle. When the scheme is `fourDirectional`, draw the
  current invariant hexagon unchanged.
- No change to flames, ports, config, physics, or input. The cue is cosmetic
  but must be structural (deterministic vertex geometry) so it is verifiable in
  tests and identical across game/gyms.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `_redraw()` hull geometry: scheme-conditional concave rear edge; update header/comment docs.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — new Asteroids hull test (concave rear / not rotationally invariant); keep existing four-directional hexagon tests intact.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 player-hull description amended for the Asteroids concave-rear hull and the four-directional divergence.

## Related work

- AH-0MTBOIIF6004GPY8 — *Direction-neutral hexagon body shape* (completed): the design being partially reversed for the Asteroids scheme; hexagon geometry and `shipSize` semantics originate here.
- AH-0MTAF76Q1008BLBE — *Direction-neutral ship shape: circle with engines at top, bottom, and each side* (completed): origin of the neutral-hull rationale and four cardinal engine ports.
- AH-0MTBOMP93002AC25 — *Player entity tests: body shape, engine ports, per-engine flames* (completed): tests pinning the invariant hexagon; must stay green in four-directional form.
- AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD — *Alternative player control* (completed): the Asteroids/four-directional schemes and facing rotation.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 (player hull) and §2.2/§2.3 (Asteroids facing, reverse thruster, auto-fire heading).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Rendering is hard to assert in tests** (Phaser `Graphics`): mitigated by asserting deterministic vertex geometry (segment count, an interior notch vertex on the -x side) rather than pixels.
- **GDD reversal risk:** reintroducing a direction cue could re-raise the heading ambiguity the neutral hull solved; mitigated by scoping to the Asteroids scheme (which has a real facing) and documenting the scheme divergence in the GDD.
- **Notch depth ambiguity:** "subtle" is not numerically pinned. Assumption: a shallow notch (interior vertex whose distance inward from the straight rear edge is small, e.g. ≤ ~20% of the circumradius, exact value at implementation/discretion) — flag if a specific depth is wanted.
- **Assumption:** the concave notch is the only change in this item — no pointed nose, chevron/arrow redesign, new engine ports, or rotation of the four-directional hull.
- **Scope-creep guard:** pointing the four-directional hull at the velocity heading, a full arrow/chevron redesign, per-scheme config keys, or animated direction cues are **not** in scope — record as new work items if desired.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTAF76Q1008BLBE** – Direction-neutral ship shape: circle with engines at top, bottom, and each side (completed)
- **AH-0MTECNKPC00954HH** – Test: Per-scene — player/combat assertions + regression (completed)
- **AH-0MUUM1167006CXAK** – EffectsRegistry: Implement hybrid magnet logic (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: clear, currently, direction, edge, forward (+9 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: clear, currently, direction, edge, forward (+9 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: clear, direction, edge, forward, make (+7 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scheme scope:** "Which control scheme(s) get the directional hull?" — **Answer (user):** "(a) Asteroids only" — the default Asteroids scheme gets the directional hull; the four-directional scheme keeps the invariant neutral hexagon (its cardinal engine ports stay cardinal). Source: interactive reply, `/intake` session 2026-10-14.
- **Q2 — Silhouette:** "What silhouette exactly?" — **Answer (user):** "(b) Keep the hexagon outline but make only the rear edge concave (subtle cue)." Source: interactive reply, `/intake` session 2026-10-14. (Classic arrowhead (a) explicitly declined; cue must remain subtle.)
- **Q3 — Stationary nose direction:** "Which way does the nose point when stationary?" — **Answer (user):** "(a) Keep the last heading" — consistent with auto-fire's most-recent-heading fallback and the Asteroids facing. Source: interactive reply, `/intake` session 2026-10-14.
