# Side Thrusters Quieter and a Semitone Higher — Intake Brief

**Headline:** The single ship-level thruster hum plays identically for forward and sideways thrust; make the side-thruster profile 50% quieter than forward and a semitone higher pitched so lateral/turning input is audibly distinct.

## Problem Statement

The player thruster hum is a single ship-level continuous voice (`src/audio/thrusterShim.ts`) whose level depends only on the thrust magnitude — it does not distinguish which engines are firing. Turning (Asteroids) and lateral strafing (fourDirectional) therefore sound identical to forward thrust, so the manoeuvring cue is not legible by ear. The side thrusters should read as a lighter, brighter cue: **50% quieter than forward** and **a semitone higher pitched**.

## Users

- **Player** — hears the thruster hum while manoeuvring; needs forward thrust and side manoeuvring to be distinguishable without the side cue dominating the mix.

## User Stories

- As a player, when I turn or strafe using the side thrusters, I hear a quieter, higher-pitched hum than when I thrust forward, so my manoeuvring input is clear by ear.
- As a player, when I thrust forward, the thruster hum sounds exactly as it does today (volume and pitch unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Side gain is 50% of forward:** While the side-thruster profile is active, the hum's target gain at thrust level `L` is `0.5 × L × THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` — half the forward-profile target for the same `L`. Forward/default thrust remains `L × THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME`.
- **AC2 — Side pitch is one semitone higher:** The side profile shifts **both** pitched oscillators — the triangle fundamental (`THRUSTER_HUM_BASE_FREQ`, 60 Hz) and the sine undertone (`THRUSTER_HUM_UNDERTONE_FREQ`, 35 Hz) — up by one equal-tempered semitone (ratio `2^(1/12)` ≈ 1.0595), composing with the existing thrust-dependent `pitchScale`. The band-pass noise filter band (700–1100 Hz) is unchanged.
- **AC3 — Side-profile selection (operator-directed):** The side profile is selected when **any sideways engine is firing**: Asteroids `leftSide`/`rightSide` (turn left/right) and fourDirectional `left`/`right` (lateral strafe). When both a side engine and a forward/main engine are active, the **side profile wins** (quieter + higher). If no side engine is active the default (forward) profile applies. The nose retro-thruster and fourDirectional `up`/`down` use the default profile.
- **AC4 — Parity and no behavioural regressions:** The classification and profile handling are implemented **once in shared code** and behave identically in `PlayScene` and every gym scene (gym↔game parity). The hum remains a single reused voice; the beat-locked cannon-cadence modulation, growth/decay envelope, click-free retrigger, safe no-op without an `AudioContext`, and no-node-leak teardown are all preserved.
- **AC5 — Tests cover the new behaviour (testing/validation):** Unit tests pin the side profile to `0.5 ×` gain, the `2^(1/12)` pitch ratio on **both** oscillators, forward unchanged, side-wins arbitration when forward + side are held, and correct classification for both the Asteroids and fourDirectional schemes (plus the default profile for non-side engines).
- **AC6 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular the GDD §7.3 "Thruster hum" description records the side profile (volume scale, semitone pitch, arbitration rule).
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Runtime-synthesised hum only** — the thruster hum is the game's single runtime-synthesis exception; no baked asset, no new audio dependency (ToneForge/Tone.js decisions remain unchanged).
- **Single reused voice** — no second oscillator voice; the profile is an adjustment on the existing voice.
- **Side-only change** — forward/default thrust volume and pitch are unchanged.
- **Gym↔game parity** — the behaviour must be shared, not duplicated (per the repo's architecture convention).
- **Do not touch** master SFX volume/mute plumbing (`setSfxVolume`/`setSfxMuted`) or any other cue.

## Existing State

- The hum lives in `src/audio/thrusterShim.ts` (runtime synthesis exception). It exposes `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME = 0.05`, `THRUSTER_HUM_BASE_FREQ = 60`, `THRUSTER_HUM_UNDERTONE_FREQ = 35`, noise-filter bounds 700–1100 Hz, growth/decay times and beat-cadence constants.
- `updateThrusterHum(level)` computes `targetGain = level × THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME × amplitudeMod` and sets `osc.frequency = THRUSTER_HUM_BASE_FREQ × pitchScale`, `sub.frequency = THRUSTER_HUM_UNDERTONE_FREQ × pitchScale` where `pitchScale = 1 + level × 0.12`. It has **no** per-engine or forward/side distinction.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` re-exports the shim seam as `updateThrusterSound(level: number)` (thin delegation) plus the thruster constants.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` `preUpdate` calls `getEngineActivity(...)` each frame (giving the firing engine list) and separately calls `this._model.getEngineSoundLevel(...)` → `updateThrusterSound(level)`. The engine list already distinguishes ports: Asteroids `main`/`leftSide`/`rightSide`/`nose`; fourDirectional `top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right`.
- `src/utils/engineSelection.ts` (fourDirectional `enginesForThrust`/`selectEngines`) and `src/utils/movementModel.ts` (Asteroids `getEngineActivity`) are the pure, shared sources of the firing engine list. `Player.preUpdate` is shared by the game and gyms.
- `CombatCoreScene` also calls `updateThrusterSound(0)` on overlay pause (must keep working via a defaulted profile parameter).
- GDD §7.3 documents the hum as a single ship-level voice at `≤ 0.05` with beat-locked pulse; no side variant is documented.
- Existing tests: `src/audio/thrusterShim.test.ts`, `src/audio/effects.test.ts` (delegation/parity), `src/entities/Player.test.ts` (hum drive), `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (gym↔game parity guard).

## Desired Change

1. **Add side-profile constants** in `src/audio/thrusterShim.ts`: `THRUSTER_HUM_SIDE_VOLUME_SCALE = 0.5` and `THRUSTER_HUM_SIDE_PITCH_SCALE = 2^(1/12)` (≈ 1.0595), documented with units/rationale.
2. **Thread a profile** through the hum seam: extend `updateThrusterHum(level, profile?)` (and the `updateThrusterSound` re-export) with an optional profile defaulting to the forward profile so existing callers (including `CombatCoreScene`'s `updateThrusterSound(0)`) remain valid. For the side profile, multiply the gain target by the side volume scale and multiply **both** oscillator frequencies by the side pitch scale (composed with `pitchScale`); leave the noise filter untouched.
3. **Classify in shared code:** derive the profile from the firing engine list already available in `Player.preUpdate` (or a small pure helper shared by both models), selecting side when any side engine (`leftSide`/`rightSide`/`left`/`right`) is firing, side-wins over forward.
4. **Document** the side profile in GDD §7.3 and code comments; update the audio cue mapping if it references the hum.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/thrusterShim.ts` — Add `THRUSTER_HUM_SIDE_VOLUME_SCALE` / `THRUSTER_HUM_SIDE_PITCH_SCALE`; extend `updateThrusterHum` with a profile parameter; apply side gain scale and side pitch scale to both oscillators.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Extend the `updateThrusterSound` signature to forward the optional profile (backward compatible) and re-export the new constants.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Derive the forward/side profile from the firing engine list and pass it to `updateThrusterSound` (shared by game + gyms).
- `src/utils/engineSelection.ts` / `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — Shared pure helper (e.g. `isSideEngine` / `getThrusterProfile`) for side-engine classification, or extend the model's sound contract.
- `src/audio/thrusterShim.test.ts` — New tests for side gain (0.5×), semitone ratio on both oscillators, forward unchanged, and profile switching.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Delegation/parity test that the profile passes through.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — Classification tests for Asteroids turn, fourDirectional strafe, forward + side arbitration, default profile.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 "Thruster hum" documents the side profile (volume scale, semitone pitch, arbitration).
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — Update only if it references the thruster hum.
- `audio/` — **no change** (runtime synthesis; no baked asset).

## Related Work

- **AH-0MUAYB8S50029QB8** — Reduce volume of player thrusters (halved the overall hum ceiling to `0.05`; this item is a *differential* side-vs-forward change, not a duplicate).
- **AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620** — Player thruster SFX (original thruster hum implementation).
- **AH-0MUTYV9ES003A3HJ** — Thruster hum Tone.js shim (established the runtime-synthesis shim).
- **AH-0MV01G4NL009JK92** — Improve thruster audio (added the beat-locked cannon-cadence pulse).
- **AH-0MTK9ZSOX009SB1K** — Thruster hum: jet-engine roar — remove buzzy sawtooth (character/tonal decisions).
- **AH-0MTFORPJ2003RWWQ** — Asteroids directional VFX improvements (key-specific engine selection: forward→main, turn→side).
- **AH-0MTAF76Q1008BLBE** — Engine firing rule / `engineSelection.ts` (source of the firing engine list).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Single-voice arbitration:** one hum voice cannot independently represent simultaneous forward + side thrust. Operator chose **side-wins** (Q2=A); a future proportional blend would require a two-voice redesign — track as a separate item, out of scope here.
- **Perceptual subtlety:** a semitone is ≈ 6% in frequency; it may be subtle against the noise-heavy texture. The operator requested it explicitly; tests pin the ratio so the intent is verifiable even if the perceptual margin is small.
- **Assumption — fourDirectional `up`/`down` are not "side":** Q1=B scoped side to lateral left/right (fourDirectional) and turn (Asteroids). Vertical thrust is therefore treated as the default (forward) profile.
- **Assumption — nose retro-thruster is not "side":** reversed thrust uses the default profile.
- **Scope-creep risk:** changing the noise filter band, baking a side asset, or altering the beat cadence are out of scope — record any such suggestions as `discovered-from:AH-0MV78QUIX001EZN2` work items.
- **Parity risk:** implementing classification outside shared code would diverge game vs gym; the parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and a shared helper mitigate this.
- **Backward compatibility:** the new profile parameter must default to forward so `CombatCoreScene`'s `updateThrusterSound(0)` and any other callers keep compiling and behaving.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- **Q1 — Which control scheme(s) does "side thrusters" cover?** — Answer (operator, interactive): **B) Any sideways engine in both schemes** — Asteroids turn (`turnLeft`/`turnRight` → leftSide/rightSide) *and* fourDirectional `left`/`right` strafe. Source: interactive reply. (Options offered: A) Asteroids turn only; B) both schemes; C) all non-`main` engines. **Recommended:** B.)
- **Q2 — When forward and turn are held simultaneously (single hum voice), which profile wins?** — Answer (operator, interactive): **A) Side profile wins** whenever any side engine is firing. Source: interactive reply. (Options offered: A) side wins; B) forward wins; C) blend. **Recommended:** A.)
- **Q3 — What does "a semitone higher" apply to?** — Answer (operator, interactive): **A) Both pitched oscillators** (triangle 60 Hz + sine undertone 35 Hz) shifted by `2^(1/12)`; noise filter unchanged. Source: interactive reply. (Options offered: A) pitched oscillators only; B) all layers incl. noise band; C) fundamental only. **Recommended:** A.)

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D** – Symbols for weapons do not reflect what the weapon does (completed)
- **AH-0MV6T0HU0001IS71** – [test-failure] PlayScene P5 expired → fire-rate multiplier back to 1 (AC2) — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MUUJCL8J00632T7** – Boss.ts per-phase HP model, return contract, health-bar fill (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: forward, higher, make, semi, should, side, sound, them, thrusters, tone
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — matched: forward, higher, make, pitched, should, side, sound, them, thrusters, tone
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: forward, higher, make, semi, should, side, sound, them, thrusters, tone

# Game↔gym parity tests for the power-up level path

## Summary
Add parity tests that boot the **real** `GymPowerUpLeveling` gym alongside `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, resolved stats and observable effect-path outputs are identical. The parity assertion extends the shared equivalence/duplicate-body guard convention in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (or a sibling parity test co-located with it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Real-gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene (not a minimal `EquivGymScene`) alongside `PlayScene` and assert identity of the shared power-up level path.
- **AC2 — Full coverage.** For every power-up P3–P10 and a level sweep (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, resolved stats from `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, and observable effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7 teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical between gym and game.
- **AC3 — Duplicate-body guard honoured.** The parity assertion lives in the shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` remains the authoritative check; `GymPowerUpLeveling` introduces no divergent copy.
- **AC4 — Deterministic and efficient.** Tests drive `tick(dt)` only (no wall-clock); a single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots to keep parallel-suite runtime reasonable; generous Vitest timeouts for Phaser boot are acceptable.

# Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) computes a shared
balance-statistics schema for **bot** runs, but nothing aggregates the **same
statistics from human player games**. Today `npm run record` (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ)
captures raw dev-mode telemetry for a single human session, and
`npm run evaluate -- --human` does a same-seed metric comparison — but neither
produces the shared `BalanceStats` schema, so the bot cannot be validated as a
realistic proxy for a human player.

## Users

- **As a maintainer**, I want to record a human play session in dev mode and get
  the same balance statistics the bot framework produces, so I can compare the
  bot's experience against a real player's and validate that the bot is a
  realistic proxy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A **single shared pure helper** (consumed by both `npm run record` and
   `npm run evaluate -- --human`) converts a recorded human session's telemetry
   record stream into per-run `BalanceRunStats` (one per `run_header`) plus a
   `BalanceAggregate`, reusing `extractBalanceStats` and
   `aggregateBalanceStats`/`createBalanceAggregator` from the automated-balancing
   framework — no schema duplication (the shared `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`
   is used).
2. The human statistics artifact **reuses the existing `BalanceReport` shape**
   (`kind: 'balance'`) via `buildBalanceReport`, labelled with a `human`
   pseudo-policy so bot and human reports are directly comparable.
3. **Dev mode only.** Collection exists only in the dev tooling
   (`scripts/record-session.mjs` / `scripts/evaluate.mjs`); there is no change to
   production telemetry/consent config and no new production call site. No PII is
   recorded or emitted — the artifact contains only schema fields (numeric stats,
   seeds, archetype/upgrade keys, hashes).
4. When a recording contains **multiple human runs**, every run yields a per-run
   `BalanceRunStats` entry **and** one aggregate across all runs, mirroring the
   bot batch output. Output is deterministic (stable serialisation).
5. Tests cover the pure helper (single run, multiple runs, empty stream, seed
   attribution, determinism) and both tool paths (record emits the artifact,
   evaluate `--human` emits it under `--out`); a test asserts no production
   call site collects via the new path (dev-only enforcement).
6. Documentation updated (`docs/TELEMETRY.md` recording section and/or
   `docs/BALANCING.md` statistics section describe the human flow and artifact);
   full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the dev-mode recording path (`run_header` / `tick` / `event` records) — no new recording mechanism.
- Reuse the shared balance-statistics schema — same code path, not a divergent copy.
- Dev-tooling only: production telemetry/consent unchanged, no PII.
- The dev tools load the TS core via Vite SSR (as `scripts/evaluate.mjs` already does).
- Artifact shape reuses `BalanceReport` (`kind: 'balance'`, `policy: 'human'`).
- Human tickets are sampled (`sampleEveryTicks`); survival-time derivation uses
  tick numbers with the default `dtSeconds` (1/60) — report `ticks`/`dt` config
  fields are derived accordingly.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — `extractBalanceStats(records)` / `aggregateBalanceStats(points)` (pure, clock-free).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — `buildBalanceReport` / `BalanceReport` / `serialiseReport` / `fnv1aHash`.
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — `npm run record`: human session → JSONL via telemetry sink.
- `scripts/recording.mjs` — `parseRecording` splits a recording into per-run ticks/events.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — `--human` does a same-seed metric comparison (not balance stats).
- `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — `parseTelemetryJsonl` for the dev sink's flat record stream.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure helper (in `src/ai/eval/`, exported from the eval index) that
   splits a flat telemetry record stream at `run_header` boundaries and reduces
   each run through `extractBalanceStats`, aggregates via
   `aggregateBalanceStats`, and packages a `BalanceReport` (via
   `buildBalanceReport`) with `policy: 'human'`.
2. Wire `scripts/record-session.mjs` to write a `balance-stats.json` artifact
   next to the recording (or under `--out`) by loading the TS core via Vite SSR.
3. Wire `scripts/evaluate.mjs --human` to emit the same `human` `BalanceReport`
   artifact under `--out` (a pure shell over the shared helper).
4. Document the human flow + artifact in `docs/TELEMETRY.md` / `docs/BALANCING.md`.
5. Unit-test the pure helper and both tool paths; assert dev-only enforcement.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — reuse `extractBalanceStats` / `aggregateBalanceStats` (no change expected; source of the schema).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — reuse `buildBalanceReport` / `BalanceReport` (no change expected).
- `src/ai/eval/` (new pure helper, e.g. `humanStats.ts`, exported from `src/ai/eval/index.ts`) — shared human balance-statistics extraction + `BalanceReport` packaging.
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — emit the `human` `BalanceReport` artifact for `--human`.
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — write the human balance artifact next to the recording.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — surface the shared helper's artifact from `--human`.
- `src/ai/eval/humanStats.test.ts` — pure-helper tests (single/multi-run, empty, determinism).
- CLI/tool tests — record + evaluate `--human` wiring and dev-only enforcement.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/BALANCING.md` — document the human flow + artifact.

## Related work

- **Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — parent epic; defines the shared schema and bot report.
- **Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation** (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ) — `extractBalanceStats` / `aggregateBalanceStats` / `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ) — the recording path (`npm run record`, `parseRecording`).
- **Periodically validate the human experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — downstream consumer of human balance statistics.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/BALANCING.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the dev JSONL sink record stream is the canonical human source;
  splitting on `run_header` matches `parseRecording`'s run grouping.
- **Assumption:** report `ticks`/`dt`/`sampleEveryTicks` config fields for a human
  run are derived from the recording (max tick, default dt 1/60) rather than being
  meaningful bot-config values.
- **Risk:** loading the TS core from `scripts/record-session.mjs` adds Vite SSR
  coupling to the record tool — mitigate by keeping the helper pure and the shell thin.
- **Risk — scope creep:** the `--human` same-seed comparison already delivers
  metric-level deltas; this item deliberately does **not** extend that comparison
  to the balance schema (recorded as a separate opportunity, not scope).
- **Risk:** drift between bot and human extraction paths — mitigated by
  single-helper reuse and a cross-path equivalence test.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should human balance-statistics collection be wired in? (A: `npm run record`; B: `npm run evaluate -- --human`; C: both, sharing one pure helper)" — Answer (operator): **C** — both, sharing one pure helper. Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q2: "What should the human-stats artifact look like? (A: reuse `BalanceReport` with a `human` pseudo-policy; B: dedicated `{perRun, aggregate}` artifact; C: both)" — Answer (operator): **A** — reuse the existing versioned `BalanceReport` shape via `buildBalanceReport`, byte-comparable to bot reports. Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q3: "When a recording file contains multiple human runs, what should be produced? (A: per-run + one aggregate; B: aggregate only; C: latest run only)" — Answer (operator): **A** — per-run `BalanceRunStats` for every run plus one `BalanceAggregate` across all runs, mirroring bot batches. Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN** – Screen action intensity tracking and analysis (completed)
- **AH-0MV2JT3GM001BDKG** – Documentation and full-suite verification (completed)
- **AH-0MUZJDT88002L536** – Worktree builds fail: build-audio cannot resolve the sibling ToneForge CLI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv1dluz8009ocjw, absent, acceptance, add, archetype (+109 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absent, add, archetype, balance, bot (+88 more)
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — matched: 0muy08w7y004gatz, absent, acceptance, add, aggregation (+87 more)

## Plan: changelog

### 2026-10-14 — Plan decomposition (skill: plan)

- Decomposed the feature into six child work items (test-first dependency
  order), created under the parent:
  1. Human balance-statistics test suite (AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7) — task — test-first.
  2. Shared human balance-statistics helper (AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) — feature — depends on 1.
  3. Record tool emits human balance report (AH-0MV8ISOLG004KPE6) — feature — depends on 2.
  4. Evaluate --human emits human balance report (AH-0MV8ISP16004I5Z6) — feature — depends on 2.
  5. Human balance-statistics documentation (AH-0MV8ISPH8000UBD8) — docs — depends on 2.
  6. Acceptance verification and full suite (AH-0MV8ISPXN0033DPZ) — task — depends on 3, 4, 5.
- No duplicate or overlapping completed work found (searched human balance
  statistics, balance report, balance-stats.json).
- Effort/Risk pre-check returned plan (Small/Medium); existing effort-and-risk
  estimate (8.75h expected, 12.75h recommended, Medium risk) retained.
- AC-coverage review recommended `proceed`; no unresolved conflicts.

# Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation

## Target outcome
A versioned, shared balance-statistics schema (per-run + aggregate, with distribution summaries including median) extracted purely from the existing telemetry record stream, so bot and human measurements are directly comparable and downstream consumers (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN, AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) can import one schema instead of duplicating it.

## Context
The metric layer (`src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`) currently aggregates score/survival/minerals but no per-upgrade or per-archetype breakdown and no percentile/median distribution. This feature extends it with the full balance-statistics schema demanded by the epic AC3/AC4/AC5. Pure core only: no I/O, no wall clock.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New `BalanceStatistics` types (`BalanceRunStats` per-run, `BalanceAggregate` with `DistributionStats` containing count, mean, median, min, max, std-dev) are defined in `src/ai/eval/types.ts` and exported from `src/ai/eval/index.ts` with a versioned schema constant `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- `extractBalanceStats(records)` is a pure function over the telemetry record stream deriving: minerals collected, upgrades selected per choice/upgrade id, enemies killed per archetype, asteroids destroyed, power-ups collected, avoidable hits, survival time, and wave/level reached.
- `aggregateBalanceStats(points)` returns distribution summaries (count, mean, median, min, max, std-dev) per metric; median correctness verified in tests.
- Unit tests cover extraction from a synthetic record stream, aggregation incl. median/percentile correctness, empty series, and determinism; tests assert the pure core performs no I/O and never reads the wall clock.
- The schema is versioned and shared (exported), not duplicated in any sibling module.

- **Covers epic AC3:** **Full balance statistics.** The report captures, per run and aggregated, at minimum: minerals collected, upgrades selected (per upgrade/choice id), enemies killed **per archetype**, asteroids destroyed, power-ups collected, avoidable hits, survival time, and wave/level reached — with distribution summaries (count, mean, median, min, max, std-dev) across games.
- **Covers epic AC5:** **Tests.** Pure aggregation, determinism and the config-driven arena are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
## Minimal implementation
1. Extend `src/ai/eval/types.ts` with balance-statistics types and `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
2. Add `extractBalanceStats` / `aggregateBalanceStats` (and distribution helper incl. median) to `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`.
3. Export the new schema from `src/ai/eval/index.ts`.
4. Add `balanceStats.test.ts` (unit tests listed above); update `metrics.test.ts` if interfaces shift.

## Key Files
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/index.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/balanceStats.test.ts`

## Definition of done
All ACs pass; schema exported and versioned; tests green; no wall-clock/IO in the pure core.

## Target outcome
The deterministic headless arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) consumes the real balance data (enemy configs, ship config, difficulty curves) through the shared config loaders instead of the hardcoded `['scout','diver','phaser']`, fixed fire cadence and fixed ship config, so a CSV edit measurably changes simulated outcomes (epic AC1).

## Context
The arena currently hardcodes `ENEMY_FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS`, `HOSTILE_RADIUS`, `SHIP_CONFIG` and the archetype list. Verification needed: loading CSV-backed config under Node/Vite SSR (the dev path uses `fetch`/`/api/csv`, the Node shell must use the bundled/defaults or an SSR-safe loader — prototype first). Single source of truth: arena consumes `src/core/configStore.ts` / `enemyConfig.ts` / `difficultySequencer.ts` loaders; never a divergent copy of enemy or ship stats.

- The arena accepts a resolved balance-config (enemy configs, ship config, difficulty curves) via the existing config loaders (`loadAllEnemyConfigs`, `loadShipConfig`, `loadDifficultyCurves`) with no hardcoded archetype list or duplicated stats.
- A test demonstrates that changing a CSV-backed value (e.g. enemy `health` or `shotProbability`/`fireInterval`) changes the simulated outcome for the same seed.

A test demonstrates that changing a CSV value changes the simulated outcome (e.g. enemy health/`shotProbability`).

## Target outcome

# Weapon visual roster & parity guard test

Child of AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE (Variety in weapon graphics). Test-first verification item: the doc-guard-style roster test that asserts every player weapon and enemy archetype resolves a **unique** visual signature, so catalogue-wide visual identity is enforced mechanically (not by convention).

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want a roster test that asserts each of the 11 catalogue weapons and every enemy attack resolves a distinct code-drawn visual signature, so per-weapon uniqueness cannot regress silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Every player weapon is visually unique in flight.** Each of the 11 catalogue weapons (`cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova, mortar, arc`) has a distinct code-drawn projectile shape and/or per-shot VFX that differs from every other weapon; a doc/roster test asserts catalogue-wide uniqueness. The Wave Laser (and Dual) must render as a line/beam, **not** a dot.
- **Every enemy attack has its own projectile identity.** One child per enemy weapon (Scout/Invader aimed shot, Diver spread burst, Tank radial, Phaser radial, Swarm burst, Raider shot, Boss spread, Boss spiral, Boss pulse, Boss desperation, Capturer tractor beam, Orbital-Strike falling shell) — each with a distinct shape/colour/feel reflecting its archetype and gated by its existing fire behaviour (visuals/feel only; firing logic, speeds, intervals and patterns unchanged).
- **Per-weapon game feel.** Each weapon/attack child adds VFX **and** SFX for both fire and impact (muzzle flash / launch cue, trail where appropriate, impact flash + hit sound), consistent with the code-drawn neon aesthetic and the existing baked-cue audio pipeline (ToneForge `playCue`).
- **Gym↔game parity.** Every gameplay-visual change is applied through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, shared entities/utils) and consumed identically by the relevant gym scene(s) and `PlayScene`; the repo duplicate-body guard and gym-parity assertions must pass unchanged. No behaviour/balance re-tuning (fire rates, beat grid, speeds, damage, ranges stay as-is).
- **Full test suite passes** with the new changes, including updated graphics command-buffer tests and new per-weapon visual/audio tests.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts` (new, alongside existing docs-guard tests)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — catalogue + shape metadata the test consumes
- `src/entities/bulletUtils.ts` — enemy shape resolver the test consumes

## Dependencies

- Parent: AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE
- Written first (test-first); must pass once the shared seam + all weapon children land.

## Scope guard

Test/verification item only — no production behaviour change.

# Shared bullet-shape rendering seam

Child of AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE (Variety in weapon graphics). The data-driven rendering seam that lets each weapon id and enemy archetype resolve its own code-drawn projectile shape(s), VFX config and feel, consumed identically by `PlayerBullet` and `bulletUtils` in the game and every gym. Most weapon children depend on this.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want one shared, parity-safe shape resolver so per-weapon and per-archetype bullet visuals live in a single seam the game and every gym consume identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Every player weapon is visually unique in flight.** Each of the 11 catalogue weapons (`cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova, mortar, arc`) has a distinct code-drawn projectile shape and/or per-shot VFX that differs from every other weapon; a doc/roster test asserts catalogue-wide uniqueness. The Wave Laser (and Dual) must render as a line/beam, **not** a dot.
- **Every enemy attack has its own projectile identity.** One child per enemy weapon (Scout/Invader aimed shot, Diver spread burst, Tank radial, Phaser radial, Swarm burst, Raider shot, Boss spread, Boss spiral, Boss pulse, Boss desperation, Capturer tractor beam, Orbital-Strike falling shell) — each with a distinct shape/colour/feel reflecting its archetype and gated by its existing fire behaviour (visuals/feel only; firing logic, speeds, intervals and patterns unchanged).
- A shape resolver exists that draws into a Phaser `Graphics` context from visual metadata and supports at least: disc, line/beam, teardrop/streak, missile, ring, shell, jagged bolt; `BulletShape` in `src/utils/weapons.ts` extends beyond `'circle' | 'line'`, and `weaponLevels.ts` carries the new fields through level resolution without changing upgrade values.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Every gameplay-visual change is applied through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, shared entities/utils) and consumed identically by the relevant gym scene(s) and `PlayScene`; the repo duplicate-body guard and gym-parity assertions must pass unchanged. No behaviour/balance re-tuning (fire rates, beat grid, speeds, damage, ranges stay as-is).
- Per-shot VFX stay cheap: small Graphics primitives, short lifetimes, reusing `src/vfx/` conventions.
- **Full test suite passes** with the new changes, including updated graphics command-buffer tests and new per-weapon visual/audio tests.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — per-shape rendering driven by weapon definition
- `src/entities/bulletUtils.ts` — shared enemy-bullet creation; per-archetype shape seam
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — extend `BulletShape`/`WeaponDefinition` with visual metadata
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — carry visual fields through level resolution
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact hooks
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `GymFodderEnemies.ts`, `GymBoss.ts` — adopt the shared seam (parity)

## Dependencies

- Parent: AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE
- Prerequisite for every weapon/attack child.

## Scope guard

Seam/infrastructure only; register signature look-ups, do not re-tune any weapon behaviour.

# Cannon — projectile identity, VFX & SFX

Child of AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE (Variety in weapon graphics). Visuals-only: gives the `cannon` player weapon a distinct in-flight projectile look, per-shot VFX and fire/impact SFX through the shared bullet-shape seam.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the Cannon's shots to render as a compact neon disc with a short fading trail and a clean muzzle flash, so I can read at a glance which weapon I am holding and feel it when it fires and connects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Every player weapon is visually unique in flight.** Each of the 11 catalogue weapons (`cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova, mortar, arc`) has a distinct code-drawn projectile shape and/or per-shot VFX that differs from every other weapon; a doc/roster test asserts catalogue-wide uniqueness. The Cannon shot is a compact neon disc with a short fading trail and a clean muzzle flash.
- **Per-weapon game feel.** Each weapon/attack child adds VFX **and** SFX for both fire and impact (muzzle flash / launch cue, trail where appropriate, impact flash + hit sound), consistent with the code-drawn neon aesthetic and the existing baked-cue audio pipeline (ToneForge `playCue`). The Cannon's fire cue is existing `playWeaponFireSound` cue reused (already present) and its impact cue is newly baked ToneForge impact cue.
- Fire VFX (muzzle flash / launch cue) and any trail for `cannon` are wired through the shared combat-core spawn path as cheap Graphics primitives in the `src/vfx/` style.
- A distinct impact flash + hit sound plays when a `cannon` shot connects, routed through the shared impact path so game and gyms behave identically.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Every gameplay-visual change is applied through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, shared entities/utils) and consumed identically by the relevant gym scene(s) and `PlayScene`; the repo duplicate-body guard and gym-parity assertions must pass unchanged. No behaviour/balance re-tuning (fire rates, beat grid, speeds, damage, ranges stay as-is).
- **Full test suite passes** with the new changes, including updated graphics command-buffer tests and new per-weapon visual/audio tests.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — per-shape rendering driven by the weapon definition
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `cannon` visual metadata (shape/visual fields)
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — carry visual fields through level resolution unchanged
- `src/audio/effects.ts` + `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` — fire/impact cues
- `src/vfx/` — `cannon` muzzle/trail/impact module(s)
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact hooks
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` + `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — parity adoption

## Dependencies

- Parent: AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE
- Shared bullet-shape rendering seam (prerequisite child)

## Scope guard

Visuals/feel only. Any behaviour/balance change discovered while adding feel must be filed as a separate work item (`related-to:AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE`), not absorbed here.

data.description:
# Unit tests: recharge-time level axes

## Goal

Verify the new recharge-time level axes resolve correctly before implementation (test-first; drives the catalogue implementation feature). A player's recharge time is level-derived; these tests pin the maths so the later engine and HUD work on a verified foundation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `phaseRechargeRate` and `teleportRechargeRate` resolve deterministically from `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at every level 0..8, monotonic non-decreasing and clamped to their caps (Phase Shift base 1/30 → cap 1/10 charges/s; Teleport base 1/15 → cap 1/5).
- Level-up reduces recharge time: the seconds inverse (`1/rate`) decreases with level — 30 → 10 s for Phase Shift and 15 → 5 s for Teleport — and a higher level never recharges slower than a lower level.
- `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` reports a positive delta for the rate axes between levels (using the catalogue label/unit) and omits them once the curve has flattened.
- The axes are members of `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` in catalogue order; the existing catalogue-completeness and monotonicity suites still pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` with a recharge-axes describe block (resolution, monotonicity, caps, seconds inverse, change-summary deltas).
- No production code changes in this item (test-first) — the suite stays red until the implementation feature lands.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first item; the implementation feature is dependency-wired to this item).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts

data.description:
# Recharge-time level axes in the power-up catalogue

## Goal

Add the two recharge-time axes to the single power-up level catalogue (AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6), reusing the shared exponential-saturation curve — no new curve implementation. Producer decision (plan Q1): the axes are stored as increasing **rates** (charges/s) so the monotonic non-decreasing invariant holds; the AC's seconds are exposed at point of use as `1/rate`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New level variables `phaseRechargeRate` (base 1/30 → cap 1/10 charges/s) and `teleportRechargeRate` (base 1/15 → cap 1/5) exist in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` with label/unit/description/rationale, resolved through the shared exponential-saturation curve — no new curve implementation.
- Level-up reduces recharge time: `phaseRechargeTime()` and `teleportRechargeTime()` (the seconds inverse `1/rate`) decrease with level — 30 → 10 s for Phase Shift and 15 → 5 s for Teleport — recharge time is level-derived and higher levels recharge faster.
- `PowerUpLevelVariable`, `PowerUpLevelStats` and `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` include the new axes; both resolve monotonic non-decreasing and clamped to cap; neither is listed in `DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`.
- `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` surfaces the rate deltas in the hold-full change summary.
- The GDD power-up levelling table (§4.4) lists the two new axes with their base/cap values.

## Minimal Implementation

# Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore

## Goal

Implement the run-scoped per-charge recharge model in the single `PowerUpLevelStore`: every consumed Phase Shift / Teleport charge starts its own timer and returns when the level-derived time elapses, capped at 3, and the permanent Phase Shift hold-full reward is converted from unlimited activations to a recharging pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-charge recharge model: `consumePhaseCharge()` / `consumeTeleport()` start one independent recharge timer per consumed charge; when the level-derived time elapses the charge returns to the pool; a charge that has recharged and been spent again starts a new timer.
- Maximum charge cap of 3: the pool never exceeds 3 charges for either ability, whether collected (field pickup / hold-full reward) or recharged. Any collection or recharge that would exceed the cap is discarded.
- Level-up reduces recharge time: recharge time is level-derived via `phaseRechargeRate`/`teleportRechargeRate`; `phaseRechargeTime()`/`teleportRechargeTime()` expose seconds (`1/rate`) so higher levels recharge faster.
- Permanent Phase Shift is a recharging pool: the hold-full reward no longer grants unlimited activations; it adds one charge (up to the cap of 3) and recharges like any other charge.
- Field pickup grants one charge: collecting Phase Shift or Teleport from the field grants the level-derived grant count (`phaseCharges`/`teleportStacks` from the level catalogue), clamped so the total never exceeds 3.
- Teleport hold-full mirrors Phase Shift: +1 charge, clamped to 3, recharging normally.
- Recharge timers are run-scoped: they advance while the game runs and are cleared by `reset()` with the level store (weapon parity).

## Minimal Implementation

- `PowerUpLevelStore`: per-charge recharge-timer state, `tickRecharge(dt)`, grant/consume clamping (collect field/hold-full, recharge-complete), seconds accessors, redefinition of `_phasePermanent` as an owned flag (not unlimited), `reset()` clearing.
- Update module-header docs to describe the recharge model.

## Dependencies

- Unit tests: per-charge recharge engine and cap-3 (test-first).
- Recharge-time level axes in the power-up catalogue (axes + seconds accessors).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts

As a developer refactoring the bot's physics model, I want a test harness that

# Live thruster config carried in BotSnapshot

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

`BotSnapshot` must carry the player's live thruster physics — forward
`thrustAcceleration`, `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration` and reverse
`enabled` / `reverseAcceleration` / `reverseMaxSpeed` — sourced from the live
`Player`/`ShipConfig` via `buildBotSnapshot`, not from tunables.

As a player who tuned my ship, I want the demo bot to receive my live thruster
configuration in its decision input, so the bot flies the same physics I
configured without any code edits.

## Scope

- Add a public `Player.getThrusterConfig()` getter returning the forward and
  reverse thruster physics, mirroring the existing `getRotationConfig()`
  precedent (reads the live/effective `_config`).
- Extend `BotPlayer` in `botSnapshot.ts` (nested `thruster` object or
  flattened fields) and populate it in `buildBotSnapshot` via the structural
  `BotPlayerSource` seam — only when the source exposes it, so snapshots from
  sources without the getter keep their existing shape.
- Ensure the derived `BotWorld.player` and the pure decision layer receive the
  config unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Player.getThrusterConfig()` returns forward thrust acceleration, max speed and friction deceleration, plus reverse enabled / acceleration / max speed, mirroring the `getRotationConfig()` precedent.

# implement.py finish build step times out at 300 s (npm run build ~5 min due to audio render)

## Headline

The `implement.py finish` build gate aborts work items whose `npm run build`
exceeds the hard-coded 300 s timeout; on this repo the build takes ~5 min
because `build-audio` auto mode always re-renders all 65 baked WAVs. The fix:
make `build-audio` verify committed assets first and only re-render when the
audio inputs have actually changed, so the build is near-instant unless audio
sources moved.

## Problem

`run_build()` in `implement.py` executes `npm run build` with a fixed
`timeout=300`. On this repo `npm run build` runs `build-audio` (in default
`auto` mode), which **unconditionally re-renders every baked ToneForge
asset** whenever the ToneForge CLI is resolvable — measured 3.5–6 min for the
audio stage alone (machine-load dependent), plus `tsc --noEmit` (~7 s) and
vite build. `implement.py finish` therefore routinely aborts with
`Command '['npm', 'run', 'build']' timed out after 300 seconds` even though
the build itself is green, blocking finish for every work item that touches
the build.

The rendered output is **byte-deterministic**: re-rendering matches the
committed assets and checksums (a full build leaves no dirty tree). The only
defect is the wasted re-render and the wrapper timeout.

## Users

- **Implementing agent** running `implement.py finish <id>` — wants the
  automated build gate to pass when the build is genuinely green.
- **Producer/developer** working this repo — wants fast local builds and CI
  that does not re-render unchanged audio.
- **Repo maintainers of the audio pipeline** (future cue/recipe authors) —
  want a change to manifest/recipes/pin to still force a re-render.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `implement.py finish <id>` completes its build step without a spurious
  timeout on this repo (a ~5 min render no longer blocks finish).
- A fresh `npm run build` produces a **byte-identical artifact set**
  (committed WAVs + `checksums.json` unchanged) when no audio inputs changed.
- When any audio input (manifest, recipe, pin, seed block) changes,
  `build-audio` re-renders and the assets + checksums update deterministically.
- `--verify` still performs a strict checksum-only verification; explicit
  `--render` still forces a full re-render; auto mode's fast path is
  verifiable and documented.
- Existing audio pipeline tests pass; new tests cover the verify-first fast
  path (unchanged inputs → no render) and the changed-input re-render path.
- All related documentation updated (build-audio header comments, usage text,
  any docs referencing the auto-mode behaviour).
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must stay within the built-in determinism contract: assets are rendered
  twice and compared; re-render must produce identical checksums.
- `build-audio` fast path must fail closed on any checksum drift
  (verify mismatch must still abort the build, as today).
- The fix should be repo-local (in `scripts/build-audio.mjs`), not a change
  to the global `implement.py` skill, unless a complementary safety net is
  wanted later (operator chose the verify-first fast path over the
  configurable-timeout approach).
- Auto mode's current contract — render when ToneForge CLI is available,
  else verify — is superseded by verify-when-unchanged; keep `--render`
  (`npm run build-audio:render`) and `--verify`
  (`npm run build-audio:verify`) as explicit escape hatches.
- Respect the Gym↔game parity rule: audio behaviour is pipeline-level, so no
  gameplay divergence is introduced.

## Existing state

- `package.json`: `build` = `build-audio && tsc --noEmit && vite build && check-bundle`.
- `scripts/build-audio.sh` (wrapper) → `scripts/build-audio.mjs`
  (deterministic WAV pipeline, AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD).
- `build-audio.mjs` modes: `auto` (render if ToneForge resolvable, else
  verify), `render`, `verify`. `verifyAssets()` already implements strict
  checksum verification against `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json`
  (`assets`, `seedBlock`, `manifest`), including missing/unexpected/mismatch
  detection and stale-asset removal.
- 65 baked assets under `public/audio/sfx/`, `checksums.json` version 1.
- `implement.py` (global skill at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/`, git-tracked
  in the SorraAgents repo) `run_build()` uses `timeout=300`; test/push steps
  already resolve `timeoutPerCommand` from `.pi/test-config.json`
  (SA-0MTXKIIRV009MJWG).

## Desired change

Extend `build-audio.mjs` auto mode with a **verify-first fast path**:

1. Compute a deterministic fingerprint of the audio inputs — the manifest,
   recipe files, pin, and seed block (the inputs that fully determine
   rendered output).
2. Persist that fingerprint in `checksums.json` (e.g. an `inputs` or
   `fingerprint` field written during render).
3. In auto mode: if the committed `checksums.json` fingerprint matches the
   current on-disk inputs, run `verifyAssets()` only (fast, no render) and
   succeed; otherwise fall through to the existing full render (which
   updates assets + checksums, preserving determinism).
4. `--render` and `--verify` behave exactly as today; auto mode with no
   ToneForge CLI still degrades to verify as today.

This makes `npm run build` near-instant for unchanged audio, keeps drift
detection via `verifyAssets()`, and never approaches the 300 s wrapper
timeout in practice.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Stale/absent fingerprint (rollout risk, medium).** An existing
  `checksums.json` has no fingerprint field. Auto mode must treat a missing
  or unmatchable fingerprint as "inputs may have changed" and fall through
  to render (or explicit `--verify`), never fail the build on the fast path.
- **Fingerprint completeness (medium).** The fingerprint must cover *all*
  inputs that determine output (manifest, recipe files, pin, seed block); a
  missed input would let a change slip through without re-render. Mitigation:
  compute the fingerprint over the resolved input file set used by the
  renderer (same inputs `buildAssets()` reads), and keep the derivation
  unit-tested.
- **Verify-first must stay fail-closed.** Unchanged inputs → verify only;
  any checksum mismatch still aborts the build (existing `verifyAssets`
  behaviour, unchanged).
- **Assumption: audio sources are committed/git-tracked.** The fast path
  assumes the on-disk inputs reflect the working tree; a dirty recipe with
  an unchanged fingerprint is out of scope (declared, not silent).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Parallelising the render and the global
  `implement.py` timeout config are explicitly out of scope for this item;
  record as separate work items if desired (operator chose the fast path
  only).

## Key Files

- `scripts/build-audio.mjs` — auto-mode fast path + input fingerprint logic.
- `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` — hermetic tests for fast path,
  changed-input re-render, and preserved `--verify`/`--render` semantics.
- `scripts/build-audio.d.mts` — type declarations if new exports are added.
- `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — gains the persisted input fingerprint.
- `package.json` — no script change expected (or document if `build-audio`
  default flag changes).

## Related work

- `AH-0MV880FUX003TB9E` — Implement build gate times out on the ~5-minute
  ToneForge audio render (open near-duplicate; closed as duplicate per
  operator decision — its "document the chosen mechanism" AC is folded into
  this item).
- `AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD` — Deterministic WAV build pipeline (builds the
  module being changed; completed).
- `AH-0MUZJDT88002L536` — Worktree builds fail: build-audio cannot resolve
  the sibling ToneForge CLI (completed; resolved ToneForge resolution in
  worktrees, context for auto-mode behaviour).
- `AH-0MUZ5HW310018DQR` — CI: Pages deploy npm ci fails under npm 10 due to
  file: ToneForge optional dependency (completed).
- `AH-0MUTYVA2C000SNPO` — Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene (completed;
  pin-check runs before auto mode).
- `SA-0MTXKIIRV009MJWG` — global implement.py per-repo timeout config
  precedent (referenced in code).
- `SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0` — Local skill extensions for global skills
  (the alternative repo-local extension mechanism; not needed for this
  fix since the change lives in the repo's own build scripts).

### Related work (automated report from /skill:find-related)

- **AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T** – Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme
  and accept headerless CSV seed format (completed).
- **AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW** – GymDiver AC1 (diver x locked during dive) is
  wall-clock flaky under full-suite parallel load (completed; repository
  build/test-timing context).
- **AH-0MUTYV8RJ009MWKJ** – Audio playback contract tests (completed;
  audio output contract relevant to the baked-asset pipeline).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Two open work items describe the same 300 s build-gate timeout with
  overlapping ACs (`AH-0MV87694J009Z34V`, older/high priority/cross-referenced;
  `AH-0MV880FUX003TB9E`, later/medium). How should they be consolidated?"
  — Answer (operator, interactive): "A: Keep this item, close
  `AH-0MV880FUX003TB9E` as duplicate." Recommended option A matched.
- Q2: "Which fix approach? A) verify-only fast path in build-audio when
  committed assets match; B) configurable build timeout in implement.py;
  C) both; D) parallelise the render."
  — Answer (operator, interactive): "A" — verify-only fast path in
  `build-audio`, repo-local, root-cause fix. Recommended option A matched.
  (Option B was noted as an acceptable future safety net, not taken now.)

# Intake Brief — Make the level/wave banner background semi-transparent and extend its duration

## Problem statement

The centred level/wave announcement banner has an opaque black background, so
during the brief pause **between levels/waves it hides the action on screen**
(carried-over asteroids keep moving, enemies are still alive). Players cannot
see what is happening behind the banner. The banner also clears too quickly to
read comfortably.

## Users

- **Player** — *"As a player, I want the level/wave banner to let me see the
  field behind it while I read the announcement, and to stay on screen long
  enough to read."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The level/wave banner background is **60 % opaque** (alpha ≈ `0.6`) instead
   of fully opaque, for both the level-start announcement and the
   wave-transition banner.
2. The banner stays visible for **3.5 s** (current 1.5 s + 2 s) for both the
   level-start announcement and the wave-transition banner, then hides
   automatically as before.
3. Both the background alpha and the duration are exported constants (e.g.
   `BANNER_BACKGROUND_ALPHA`, `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS`) so tests can pin
   them.
4. Existing tests that assert the old 1.5–2 s hide timing
   (`AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN AC1/AC2`, `AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV AC6`) are updated to
   the new 3.5 s window, and a test asserts the semi-transparent background.
5. GDD §3 (level-progression transient-banner wording) is updated to the new
   3.5 s window; the constant's doc comment no longer claims the ~1.5–2 s
   requirement.
6. The full project test suite passes with the changes (no dead
   constants/parameters left behind).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** the banner exists **only** in `PlayScene` (no gym
  renders it), so no gym-scene change is required.
- **Readability:** the semi-transparent background must keep the white banner
  text legible against gameplay; at 60 % the existing 34 px monospace text with
  `padding {x: 20, y: 12}` is unchanged.
- The banner must remain **transient** — it still expires on its own (just
  after 3.5 s), per the GDD's "transient transitions" principle
  (AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN).
- Phaser `TextStyle.backgroundColor` takes a CSS colour string; alpha must be
  expressed as `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` (verify it renders in Phaser 4.2.1 — if
  unsupported in the canvas fill path, use `setBackgroundColor('rgba(...)')`
  or a `Graphics` rectangle behind the text).

## Existing state

- `BANNER_STYLE` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:338`) sets
  `backgroundColor: '#000000'` — fully opaque.
- `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS = 1.5` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:301`); its doc
  comment says the value "must be within the ~1.5–2 s window required by
  AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN" — this changes to 3.5 s.
- The level-start announcement (`_announceLevel`) and the wave-transition
  banner (`_updateTransitionBanner`) both call the shared `_showBanner`, so a
  single duration/alpha change covers both surfaces.

## Desired change

- Set `backgroundColor: 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)'` in `BANNER_STYLE` (or the
  equivalent alpha-based background) so the field remains visible.
- Raise `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` to `3.5` and update its doc comment to drop
  the old ~1.5–2 s constraint.
- Update the existing banner-timing tests to the new window and add a test
  pinning the semi-transparent background.
- Update GDD §3 wording for the new banner window.

## Acceptance-criteria coverage of existing tests

The following existing tests hard-code the old 2 s hide window and must be
updated with this change:
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` `AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN AC1` (`tick(2.0)` →
  hidden) and `AC2` (reappears + hides again).
- `AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV AC6` "level-name banner remains transient" (`tick` at
  2 s / 2 s + 0.5 s expect visible-then-hidden).

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `BANNER_STYLE` background and
  `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` (+ doc comment).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — update banner-timing tests; add
  semi-transparent-background assertion.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §3 transient-banner wording for the new
  3.5 s window.

## Related work

- AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN — "Level transition banner persists for the whole wave"
  (established the transient ~1.5–2 s hide behaviour this item extends).
- AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV — "Show the level name in the level-start banner"
  (banner content/transience tests this item must keep passing).
- AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2 — "Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K'"
  (established the banner label text).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2** – Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K' (completed)
- **AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN** – Level transition banner persists for the whole wave (completed)
- **AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV** – Show the level name in the level-start banner (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: also, background, banner, hard, level (+11 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: also, banner, hard, level, levels (+9 more)
- `README.md` — matched: also, background, hard, level, levels (+9 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "visible for 2 seconds longer" means the current 1.5 s
  duration is increased **to 3.5 s** (1.5 + 2). If the intent was a 2 s total,
  only the constant and GDD wording change — flag before implementation.
- **Risk (medium):** Phaser 4.2.1 `TextStyle.backgroundColor` support for
  `rgba()` CSS strings must be verified; fallback is a `Graphics` rectangle
  behind the text or `setBackgroundColor('rgba(0,0,0,0.6)')`. Covered by the
  automated background assertion in AC4.
- **Risk (low):** extending the banner window to 3.5 s lengthens the time the
  centred text covers the playfield; the 60 % transparency (not full removal)
  keeps the field visible while retaining the GDD "transient" principle.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no follow-up opportunities were observed during
  intake; if a larger banner redesign (animation, fade, resizing) is requested
  later, it should be tracked as a separate work item, not folded in here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How transparent should the banner background be?" — Answer
  (operator): "60 % opacity". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Should the +2 s apply to both the level-start announcement and the
  wave-transition banner?" — Answer (operator): "Both". Source: interactive
  reply. Note: both surfaces share `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` via `_showBanner`,
  so a single constant change covers both.
- Q3: "How should the GDD §3 '~1.5–2 s transient' wording be handled?" —
  Answer (operator): "Update GDD". Source: interactive reply.
- Research summary: inspected `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`BANNER_STYLE`,
  `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS`, `_showBanner`) and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
  banner tests; `wl search "banner"` surfaced the related items above. No gym
  scene renders the banner (gym-parity check performed). Phaser version is
  4.2.1; `rgba()` in `TextStyle.backgroundColor` to be verified at
  implementation time (constraint noted).

# Intake brief — Smart Bomb is too powerful

## Problem statement

The Smart Bomb power-up (Defender homage, AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ) is too strong: a hold-full reward makes its screen-wide pulse repeat every **5 seconds** at base level (and up to every 2 s at the cap), and its pulse radius (1200 → 2400 px) already exceeds the whole 960×540 play field from the first pickup. The result is a near-continuous screen clear that trivialises every wave the moment the permanent smart bomb is earned.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the smart bomb to stay a tense "panic button" (rare, high-value wake-up) rather than a passive auto-win.

**User story:** "As a player who earned the permanent smart bomb from the hold-full choice, I want it to pulse rarely (once every ~30 seconds at first, never more often than once per 10 seconds) and to cover only a modest area around my ship, so the game stays challenging instead of auto-playing."

## Desired change

1. **Pulse rate (permanent smart bomb only):** fire every `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` seconds — 30 s on the first grant (level 0), −2 s per further level, floor 10 s. A field pickup (one-shot) still fires exactly once on collection.
2. **Pulse radius (both permanent and runtime-collected):** base = **200 px** (10 × `SHIP_SIZE` = 10 × 20), additive **+2 % of base per level** → `min(400, 200 × (1 + 0.02 × level))`, capped at 400 px (2× base). No longer screen-wide.
3. **Damage unchanged:** stays 1 → 3 HP per pulse (no change).
4. Resolved through the same shared `AoEDescriptor`/`screenPulse` seam so the game and every gym run identical code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A permanent smart bomb pulses on the interval `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` seconds: 30 s at level 0 (first grant), 28 s at level 1, … 10 s at level 10 and beyond; `smartBombInterval()` reflects this schedule.
- The smart bomb pulse radius resolves to `min(400, 200 × (1 + 0.02 × level))` px: 200 px base (10× ship size), additive +2 % of base per level, capped at 400 px. Applies to both permanent pulses and one-shot field pickups.
- Smart bomb damage per pulse is unchanged (1 → 3 HP across levels).
- Behaviour lands in the shared core (`effects.ts` / `powerUpLevels.ts` + the AoE seam) so `PlayScene` and the gym scenes (`GymPowerUpsCombat` and the shared `powerUpLeveling.parity` tests) run identical code — no divergent copies.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular, "screen-wide" descriptions of the pulse must be corrected in `docs/Game Design Document.md` and `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` (§6).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (including updated `powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `effects.test.ts` and `AoeWeapons.test.ts` assertions that pin the old 1200/2400 px and 0.2→0.5/s values).

## Constraints

- The level model in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` currently stores every variable on the `exponential-saturation` curve (`src/utils/curve.ts`; the `UpgradeCurve` union has a single member). The two new schedules — linear-descending interval and linear-additive radius — are **not expressible** by that curve, so a new curve type (e.g. a linear/clamped variant) must be added to `src/utils/curve.ts` and consumed by the smart-bomb specs. Keep the resolver pure, deterministic, monotonic and clamped as today.
- The pulse-frequency axis is stored non-decreasing (`smartBombFrequency`, pulses/s); the desired *interval* schedule is descending, so represent the change as `frequency = 1 / max(10, 30 − 2×level)` (non-decreasing, meets the model's monotonicity contract) or restructure the variable — implementation choice, but `smartBombInterval()` must return the documented schedule.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): the change must be applied once in the shared core and consumed by both sides; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard in `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` enforces this.
- `SHIP_SIZE = 20` (`src/core/constants.ts`) is the ship-size base used by the magnet convention (`magnetRadius`), and 10× of it = **200 px** (operator decision Q1-A).

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.smart_bomb`: `aoeRadius` base 1200/cap 2400 (k=0.3, exponential-saturation), `smartBombDamage` base 1/cap 3, `smartBombFrequency` base 0.2/cap 0.5 (k=0.3).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `isSmartBombPermanent()`, `smartBombFrequency()`, `smartBombInterval()`, `smartBombAoe()`, `updateSmartBomb(dt)`; permanent pulse timer.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_updateSmartBomb(dt)` consumes `smartBombAoe()` and applies it through the shared AoE seam; `CombatScene.onSmartBombPulse`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `SHIP_SIZE = 20`.
- Tests pinning current values: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` (102–107, 136–163), `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (~596–656), `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` (~810–866).

## Key Files

- `src/utils/curve.ts` — new linear/clamped curve type (currently only `exponential-saturation`).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — re-spec the three smart-bomb variables (radius schedule, frequency/interval schedule; damage unchanged) with the new curve.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `smartBombInterval()` / `smartBombAoe()` resolve the new schedules; comments updated.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — only if the seam needs adjustment (expected: none).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — possibly a named constant for the 10× ship-size / 2 % tuning knobs.
- Tests: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

## Related work

- AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ — Defender smart bomb pulse (the original feature being re-balanced; completed).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — Design level curves for all power-ups (the model this change extends).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention (must be preserved).
- AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4 — Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch (adjacent pickup behaviour; completed).
- AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4 / AH-0MV1BIUGE005BJO8 — classic power-up research epics that introduced the smart bomb (background).

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ** – Defender smart bomb pulse (completed)
- **AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4** – Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch (completed)
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `README.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`

## Risks & assumptions

- **Curve-family extension risk:** adding a linear/clamped curve to `src/utils/curve.ts` touches shared machinery used by all levelled variables — the new curve must stay pure/deterministic and unit-tested so it cannot regress weapon or other power-up curves. Mitigation: new curve type is additive; existing specs keep `exponential-saturation`; parity/equivalence tests guard the seam.
- **Value-inversion risk:** switching the smart-bomb axis meaning (interval vs frequency) could break `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` / hold-full overlay deltas or the monotonicity contract — keep frequency non-decreasing (`1/interval`) and clamp, and pin expected resolved values in `powerUpLevels.test.ts`.
- **Scope creep:** opportunities observed during implementation (e.g. retuning the *Bomb* power-up, smart bomb visual redesign for a smaller radius) must be recorded as linked work items, not absorbed into this item.

## Assumptions

- "lvl1" in the request maps to **level 0** (first collection) in the code's level semantics — i.e. the base schedule is 30 s and the basic radius is 200 px at first pickup.
- Interval applies only to the *permanent* (hold-full) smart bomb; the one-shot field pickup fires once regardless.
- Damage tuning (1 → 3) is out of scope for this change.
- Radius cap of 2× base (400 px) is acceptable (operator decision Q2-A); radius growth is **additive** (+2 % of base per level).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "10× the radius of the ship: what is the base radius?" — Answer (operator): **A — 10 × SHIP_SIZE = 200 px**, matching the magnet/scoop "× ship size" convention (`magnetRadius` uses `shipSize` as the base unit). Source: interactive reply to intake round 1. Research: `src/core/constants.ts` `SHIP_SIZE = 20`; `src/powerups/effects.ts` `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)`.
- Q2: "2 % every lvl: additive or compound, and cap?" — Answer (operator): **A — additive** `base × (1 + 0.02 × level)`, **cap 2× base = 400 px**. Source: interactive reply. Research: current `powerUpLevels.ts` variables are monotonic non-decreasing with infinite level space, so a finite cap is required by the model's clamping contract.
- Q3: "Confirm interval schedule `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` with level 0 = first pickup, and damage unchanged?" — Answer (operator): **Confirmed.** Source: interactive reply. Research: `effects.ts` `updateSmartBomb`/`smartBombInterval` (permanent only); field pickup path is one-shot.

# Stop ignoring standups/ so the standup skill can version report history

## Problem

The standup skill (global) auto-commits and pushes each generated daily report so standup history is versioned. It uses a surgical git add of only the report file followed by commit and push.

In this repo standups/ is ignored in two places:

- .gitignore line ~50: standups/ under the comment "Generated daily standup reports (automated artefacts, never committed)"
- .git/info/exclude: a machine-local entry added as a bootstrap until .gitignore lands on dev

Because the path is ignored, git add silently skips the report file and the script's commit becomes a silent no-op — standup history is never versioned. Observed 14th Oct 2026: standups/2026_10_14.md was written but the commit failed with "The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: standups".

## Background / conflicting prior decision

AH-0MU480XW8009160C (completed, v0.1.4, commit 0cd5984) deliberately added the .gitignore entry to stop generated reports dirtying the working tree, which blocked the implement skill's dirty-tree gate. Since then the standup skill moved to the auto-commit strategy: reports are created once per day and committed immediately, so the tree-cleanliness concern no longer applies to the standalone report files. The skill docs explicitly identify the ignore as a stopgap that makes the commit a silent no-op (SA-0MUDYRHVZ005PQP4).

## Scope

In scope:
- Remove the standups/ entry (and its explanatory comment) from .gitignore.
- Remove the standups/ entry from the machine-local .git/info/exclude.
- Backfill history: commit the existing generated reports already on disk so the versioned standup history starts now.
- Re-run the standup script to confirm the commit-and-push path now works.

Out of scope: changing how/when the standup report is generated; touching other repos' ignore rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: standups/ no longer appears in .gitignore or .git/info/exclude.
- [ ] AC2: Existing report files on disk are tracked in git and pushed to dev.
- [ ] AC3: Re-running the standup generator commits and pushes the report (no "paths are ignored" warning).
- [ ] AC4: git status --porcelain is clean after the generator run (no stray dirty state introduced).
- [ ] AC5: All tests pass (npm test).
